data.title: Most Illinois farmland is not owned by farmers
data.author: NaOH
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了伊利诺伊州农田所有权的变化及其对农民的影响。汉斯·毕晓普曾在其父亲的土地上经营一个可持续的蔬菜农场，但由于父亲退休和地主要求，他不得不放弃种植蔬菜，改回种植玉米和大豆，并使用农药和化肥。文章指出，伊利诺伊州大部分农田为租赁性质，越来越多农地被企业收购，导致小农和可持续农业面临挑战。农田租金上涨和企业投资增加使得个人拥有农地愈发困难，缺乏对企业收购的限制可能进一步加剧这一问题。同时，气候变化和西部水资源短缺使伊利诺伊农地成为更具吸引力的投资选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：农田所有权与经营权的不同模式及其影响

不同观点：
• **农田所有权与经营权分离的普遍性**：
  - [arbor_day] 指出，在伊利诺伊州，许多农田由有限责任公司（LLC）拥有，而不是农民个人，目的是为了降低风险和便于传承。农田经常通过法律实体代代相传。
  - [dlcarrier] 支持这种模式，认为垂直整合有其优势，且由于法规的复杂性，拥有公司比直接拥有资产更易于管理。他以小飞机的所有权为例说明这一点。
  - [legitster] 认为，农田由农民自己拥有的经济优势明显，因为农民能享受税收减免和政府补贴，但承认这种情况在伊利诺伊州虽然有限但正在增加。

• **农田所有权与经营权分离的争议**：
  - [jackcosgrove] 反对将农田所有权浪漫化，指出农民将资产集中于单一的农业操作存在风险，强调农民也需要多样化投资。他还提到，历史上因为农业投资失败导致家族差点失去所有土地的例子。
  - [rjpower9000] 提到某些地主对农田的过度控制，甚至要求承租人维持单一种植模式，这种做法不仅影响生态，还限制了承租人的自主权。

• **农田所有权的地区差异**：
  - [petcat] 指出纽约州北部的情况与伊利诺伊州不同，大部分农田仍由个人和家庭拥有，且大多数是所有者自营。
  - [xnx] 强调现代农业已高度工业化，农业人口仅占总人口的1.2%，但农田所有权仍受特殊待遇，这与历史遗留的制度（如选举人团）有关。

• **税收与经济优势**：
  - [mattgrice] 提到农田在某些司法管辖区享有诸多税收优惠，包括遗产税减免和房产税豁免，这使得农田在结构化得当时具有经济吸引力。

补充讨论：
• **农田所有权与其它行业的类比**：
  - [SilverElfin] 和 [nkmnz] 都将农田所有权模式与其他行业类比，认为农民不拥有农田类似于工厂工人不拥有工厂，指出这种现象在各行各业都存在，没必要对农业特别对待。
  
• **农田传承与老龄化问题**：
  - [legitster] 和 [sophacles] 都提到农田传承的问题，许多农民年事已高，而他们的子女往往不愿意接管农场，这可能导致农田被出售给非农企业或投资者，形成农田所有权的变化。

争议焦点：
• 农田所有权是否应由农民直接拥有，以及如何平衡风险与收益。
• 农田单一种植模式的合理性，以及地主对农田操作的过度干预是否适当。
• 农业在现代社会中的地位，是否应继续享受特殊待遇。

44737353.article_content:
By
Karina Atkins
| Chicago Tribune
UPDATED:
June 2, 2025 at 3:42 PM CDT
Rain clouds pass over a cornfield owned by Farmland Reserve, May 29, 2025, in downstate Arrowsmith. Farmland Reserve, a private Salt Lake City-based  investment firm affiliated with the Mormon Church, is the largest farmland owner in Illinois. (Armando L. Sanchez/Chicago Tribune)
Surrounded by rows of soybeans and corn, Hans Bishop’s farm in central Illinois was an anomaly. He grew kale, peppers, eggplants and radishes, selling
to Whole Foods from June through October and to local restaurants, grocers and families year-round.
The vegetable farm was born in 2009 on a quarter acre rented to him by his father, a row crop farmer. After spending a decade in the corporate world, Bishop was inspired by documentaries such as
“Fresh”
and
“Food, Inc.”
that scrutinized conventional farming. He returned to the fields with aspirations to farm differently.
The fresh produce Bishop grew landed directly on chopping boards and dinner plates. It wasn’t being funneled into gasoline tanks, ultra-processed foods or livestock feed troughs — the most common destinations for Illinois’ leading agricultural products, soybeans and corn.
In less than a decade, his operation in Logan County had expanded to 80 acres. It was becoming what progressive food movements celebrate as “sustainable.”
But he couldn’t keep it going. Bishop and his wife Katie spent countless hours on marketing, had to rely on hired labor
and couldn’t access the federally subsidized safety nets available to commodity farmers.
Reporting for this story was supported by the
MIT Environmental Solutions Journalism Fellowship
.
Bishop, now 41, phased out his flourishing vegetable enterprise after his father abruptly retired in 2019, leaving him to take over the family bean and grain operation. Part of the land — 120 of the nearly 700 acres — is
rented from a family who owns multiple farm properties
and wants their fields
weed-free with perfectly straight grids of crops, a deep-rooted tradition among Midwestern farming communities.
“They want that land to be clean corn and soybeans,” Bishop said. Before the restrictions, his father was growing organic corn and soybeans on part of the field and letting Bishop grow vegetables on the rest.
Now, to keep the fields to the owner’s standards, Bishop has
had to forgo vegetables and use pesticides and fertilizers, which can pollute nearby water sources and degrade soil health over time.
Less than a fourth of Illinois farmland is owned by the farmer who works the land, according to
data
from the
Illinois Farm Business Farm Management
, a nonprofit association that helps farmers make management decisions. The rest is leased to farmers by individuals, family trusts and, increasingly, businesses.
The Tribune is launching a series of special reports analyzing the hurdles many farmers face in trying to be good stewards of the land as climate change intensifies. Among the challenges are fewer opportunities for farmers — and would-be farmers — to own their land.
Hans Bishop checks the depth of corn seed after planting, April 29, 2025, in downstate Atlanta. (Armando L. Sanchez/Chicago Tribune)
Neither the state nor the federal government maintains a centralized database of farmland ownership. The data is recorded by counties, with varying levels of detail. Some — such as Sangamon and Edgar counties — do not keep digital copies of older records.
The Tribune analyzed over 3.7 million acres of farmland in 10 counties with the most fertile soils,
highest cash rents in 2024
and available historical data. It found that over 1 in 5 acres are
owned by business entities — organizations with LLC, Inc, LTD, Co., Corp, LP and LLP tags. This is an almost 170% increase since 2005. In the same 20-year window, farmland owned by businesses with out-of-state mailing addresses increased by nearly 250%.
These acres are not necessarily owned by large conglomerates and investment firms. Corporate structures are also attractive vehicles for family businesses because they offer tax benefits and externalize losses. But, farmland is becoming a more attractive investment option as the historically fertile ground in the American West dries up.
“Water availability threatens farmland in the
Central Valley
(of California) far more than what the next 20 years of climate change will bring to Illinois,” said Illinois State Climatologist Trent Ford.
Average farmland rents in Illinois have already outstripped the inflation rate, more than doubling from
$129
to
$269
per acre per year from 2005 to 2024.
“(The rising price of land) just makes it really hard for anyone who’s not a corporation or doesn’t have that capital on hand to actually invest in that farmland,” said University of Illinois agricultural economist Brittney Kay Goodrich.
There are few guardrails to abate a corporate takeover.
Illinois is one of the only states in the Corn Belt that doesn’t place restrictions on corporate purchases of farmlan
44737353.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了伊利诺伊州农田所有权的变化及其对农民的影响。汉斯·毕晓普曾在其父亲的土地上经营一个可持续的蔬菜农场，但由于父亲退休和地主要求，他不得不放弃种植蔬菜，改回种植玉米和大豆，并使用农药和化肥。文章指出，伊利诺伊州大部分农田为租赁性质，越来越多农地被企业收购，导致小农和可持续农业面临挑战。农田租金上涨和企业投资增加使得个人拥有农地愈发困难，缺乏对企业收购的限制可能进一步加剧这一问题。同时，气候变化和西部水资源短缺使伊利诺伊农地成为更具吸引力的投资选项。
44737353.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：农田所有权与经营权的不同模式及其影响

不同观点：
• **农田所有权与经营权分离的普遍性**：
  - [arbor_day] 指出，在伊利诺伊州，许多农田由有限责任公司（LLC）拥有，而不是农民个人，目的是为了降低风险和便于传承。农田经常通过法律实体代代相传。
  - [dlcarrier] 支持这种模式，认为垂直整合有其优势，且由于法规的复杂性，拥有公司比直接拥有资产更易于管理。他以小飞机的所有权为例说明这一点。
  - [legitster] 认为，农田由农民自己拥有的经济优势明显，因为农民能享受税收减免和政府补贴，但承认这种情况在伊利诺伊州虽然有限但正在增加。

• **农田所有权与经营权分离的争议**：
  - [jackcosgrove] 反对将农田所有权浪漫化，指出农民将资产集中于单一的农业操作存在风险，强调农民也需要多样化投资。他还提到，历史上因为农业投资失败导致家族差点失去所有土地的例子。
  - [rjpower9000] 提到某些地主对农田的过度控制，甚至要求承租人维持单一种植模式，这种做法不仅影响生态，还限制了承租人的自主权。

• **农田所有权的地区差异**：
  - [petcat] 指出纽约州北部的情况与伊利诺伊州不同，大部分农田仍由个人和家庭拥有，且大多数是所有者自营。
  - [xnx] 强调现代农业已高度工业化，农业人口仅占总人口的1.2%，但农田所有权仍受特殊待遇，这与历史遗留的制度（如选举人团）有关。

• **税收与经济优势**：
  - [mattgrice] 提到农田在某些司法管辖区享有诸多税收优惠，包括遗产税减免和房产税豁免，这使得农田在结构化得当时具有经济吸引力。

补充讨论：
• **农田所有权与其它行业的类比**：
  - [SilverElfin] 和 [nkmnz] 都将农田所有权模式与其他行业类比，认为农民不拥有农田类似于工厂工人不拥有工厂，指出这种现象在各行各业都存在，没必要对农业特别对待。
  
• **农田传承与老龄化问题**：
  - [legitster] 和 [sophacles] 都提到农田传承的问题，许多农民年事已高，而他们的子女往往不愿意接管农场，这可能导致农田被出售给非农企业或投资者，形成农田所有权的变化。

争议焦点：
• 农田所有权是否应由农民直接拥有，以及如何平衡风险与收益。
• 农田单一种植模式的合理性，以及地主对农田操作的过度干预是否适当。
• 农业在现代社会中的地位，是否应继续享受特殊待遇。

data.title: Launch HN: Lucidic (YC W25) – Debug, test, and evaluate AI agents in production
data.author: AbhinavX

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lucidic工具的评价、功能、技术细节以及与竞品的比较

不同观点：
• [iancarroll] 对OpenAI默认评估系统在长会话和多次工具调用场景下的表现感到沮丧，尤其是当会话以工具调用结束时，评估结果往往较差，因为响应在下一次完成中才会出现。他还提到Go语言技术栈的 observability 工具较少，像Helicone这样与语言无关的工具更受欢迎。

• [witnessme] 对用户体验（UX）表示赞赏，但对实际的价值体验持保留态度，认为与竞争对手（如Braintrust和Opik）相比，尚未看到显著差异。

• [IgorBlink] 对调试代理的痛点表示认同，并对Lucidic的工具表示兴趣，尤其是时间旅行和轨迹聚类功能。

• [jauhar_] 对工具是否开源或是否有技术报告分享表示关注，特别感兴趣于聚类方法的结果。

• [srameshc] 表示自己并非专家，但对如何将Lucidic工具集成到现有系统中存在疑问，将其类比为代理的应用性能管理（APM）。

• [majdalsado] 正在寻找适合其初创公司的工具，并询问为何选择Lucidic而非Langfuse或Helicone。

• [henriquegodoy] 对Lucidic的UI设计提出建议，认为其UI过于“通用”，希望其更具特色。

• [simonw] 询问Lucidic如何定义“AI代理”这一术语。

• [iskhare] 对Lucidic声称其评分方法优于LLM作为裁判的说法表示好奇，希望得到详细解释。

• [KaseyZhang] 对Lucidic的聚类方法表示兴趣，希望了解更多细节。

• [barapa] 对尝试Lucidic工具表示兴奋。

• [SkylerJi] 对聚类相似响应的含义表示疑问，询问是基于精确文本相似性还是其他标准。

• [Areibman] 列举了多个由YC资助的LLMOps/AI代理 observability 产品，询问Lucidic解决了哪些其他工具未能解决的问题。

• [greatwhitenorth] 反馈前端在Pixel 8a上的使用体验不佳，建议改进响应式设计以免流失用户。

• [sharathr] 认为Lucidic是加入已经过度拥挤的 observability 工具市场的又一个新工具，对其独特性持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：工具在市场中的独特性及竞争优势。一些用户（如majdalsado和sharathr）对Lucidic相较于其他工具的独特价值表示怀疑，并提出了具体的竞品比较。

• 技术细节：用户对工具的技术实现细节（如聚类方法、定义AI代理、集成方式）表示关注，并希望得到更详细的解释。

• 用户体验：有用户（如witnessme和greatwhitenorth）对工具的实际使用体验和前端设计提出意见，表明在这些方面仍有改进空间。

data.title: Optician Sans – A free font based on historical eye charts and optotypes
data.author: exvi
data.article_summary: **Optician Sans**是一款基于历史上眼科视力表和视标设计的免费字体。它由Adobe的首席设计师Khoi Vinh主导，灵感来自1862年荷兰眼科医生Snellen创建的视力表和1959年Louise Sloan设计的无衬线字母，并根据LogMAR图表的视觉原理进行调整，以确保可读性和功能性。该字体旨在为所有用户提供最佳的可视性，包含基本拉丁字母和可选替换字符，以实现更一致的外观。Optician Sans根据SIL开放字体许可证发布，可在GitHub上免费获取，并提供相关资源用于博客或网站展示。该项目由ANTI Hamar和字体设计师Fábio Duarte Martins共同创建。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对"Optician Sans"字体的评价与相关联想

不同观点：
• [egypturnash] 认为该字体的推荐语与网页顶部的描述相似，引用了Adobe的Khoi Vinh的话，带有讽刺意味。
• [jiehong] 提到该字体让他想起一些国家的眼科图表，并提供了一个例子，指出这些图表不是基于字母阅读，而是基于方向指示。
• [dogmatism] 认为Braille Institute的Atkinson Hyperlegible字体更适合作为由视觉专家设计的字体，隐含对Optician Sans的质疑。

补充讨论：
• [cbm-vic-20] 表示主图让他的散光眼睛很不舒服，暗示字体或设计在视觉上可能存在问题。
• [gadders] 喜欢这个字体，但对包含某人的Tinder个人资料图片感到不适。
• [ayaros] 非常喜欢这个字体，并将其分享给作为眼科医生的父亲，暗示该字体在专业领域的相关性。
• [mellonaut] 提供了其他类似的字体资源，并提到某些字体的许可问题，同时指出某些字体的可读性问题。
• [htk] 喜欢这个字体，但希望有小写字母，并建议其可作为编码的固定宽度字体使用。
• [its-summertime] 认为字体中的某些字母设计（如C）容易混淆，并且模糊效果不佳，暗示设计上的不足。
• [sandbach] 对设计网站上的拼写错误感到有趣，提出对网站文本内容的质疑。
• [graypegg] 提到Snellen图表并不常见，并表达了对缺少"Optician Serif"变体的遗憾。
• [Rendello] 提供了该字体以前在新闻平台上的讨论链接，增加了背景信息。
• [amdivia] 表示加载动画让他觉得自己需要去看眼科医生，暗示动画可能引起视觉不适。
• [srameshc] 表示寻找高可读性字体，并对Optician Sans表示认可，同时提及与其他常见字体的比较。
• [voxleone] 非常喜欢这个字体，认为其在实验性和功能性之间找到了平衡，并对设计团队表示感谢。

争议焦点：
• 字体的原创性与实用性受到不同评价，部分用户对其设计细节提出质疑，而另一些用户则表示欣赏。
• 对字体的可读性和适用性存在不同看法，尤其是关于是否应包含小写字母和其视觉效果的讨论。

44736090.article_content:
OPTICIAN SANS
A free font based on the historical eye charts and optotypes used by opticians world wide.
Download for free
“Weird and wonderful”
“En elegant typeface”
“Let`s everyone act as a optician”
“Completes the eye test chart alphabet”
“A Font That Your Eye Remembers”
“A free typeface based on opticians’ eye charts”
Khoi  Vinh
Principal designer
Adobe
The LogMAR Chart is used by ophtalmologist, optometrists and vision scientist to estimate visual acuity. The chart consists of 10 letters and was developed at the National Vision Research Institute of Australia. Optician Sans is based on the same visual principles as the LogMAR chart, adjusted to be used as a fully functional display typeface.
Snellen
– 1862 –
Dutch ophthalmologist Herman Snellen developed the snellen chart in 1862. Based on a strict 5×5 unit grid. Made to measure visual acuity.
Sloan
– 1959 –
10 letters designed by Louise Sloan in 1959, following the same principles as the Snellen chart, but without the serifs. A predecessor of the logMAR charts you typically see at doctors offices today.
Optician Sans
– 2018 –
Optician Sans is a fully functional typeface and a continuation of the historical Snellen and Sloan letters. Optically adjusted for readability to be used as a fully functional display typeface.
The typeface, made with Sloan optotypes as the basis of construction, is the most effective letter selection for equal legibility. To make a typeface that ensures that all patients regardless of visual function, have the best possibility to see my commercial information, was a key goal for my new visual layout. This again shows the quality and passion I have for my profession, my practices and my patients.
Øyvind Krogh
Optometrist at Optiker-K.
Custom alternates for a more consistent look.
In addition to the basic latin characters we created a set of alternatives glyphs for a more wholesome look. How true you want to stay to the original characters is up to you. You’ll find all characters in the Glyph panel in your preferred layout or type application.
Licensing
Optician Sans is released under the SIL OPEN FONT LICENSE.
open source
Optician Sans is available on GitHub.

if you want to feature this on your blog or website.
Send us an e-mail
for more information or other requests.
Optician Sans is created by
ANTI Hamar
and typographer
Fábio Duarte Martins

data.title: Fast
data.author: gaplong
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了软件速度的重要性，尽管人们很少明确要求“快”。快速软件能改变行为，如开发者更频繁地发布代码、通过AI快速原型设计、以及通过实时流实现远程工作。相反，慢软件会限制效率，比如在飞机WiFi下难以完成任务。快的软件消除了认知摩擦，给人一种神奇的体验，如Raycast和Superhuman等工具。快还意味着简化，因为加速需要去除不必要的功能，如Linear对比Workday。实现快的过程涉及后台复杂操作，如Cash App和Instagram的优化。快也是一种乐趣，人们喜欢速度，尽管当前AI工具仍侧重功能而非性能，但未来优化将带来新能力与使用场景，改变生活。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：速度在不同领域（软件界面、编程工具、云服务、游戏等）中的重要性及其影响

不同观点：
• [hn_throwaway_99] 认为简洁快速的用户界面（如HN）能够提高使用体验，并以Slashdot的改版失败为例，指出过度追求“现代UI”可能会损害用户体验。

• [old-gregg] 通过个人职业经历说明速度可以直接影响商业利润，并强调在特定情况下，速度具有极高的商业价值。
• [ilyakaminsky] 强调在云计算环境中，速度等同于降低成本，并以自己创建转录服务的例子说明优化对服务盈利能力的重要性。
• [Liftyee] 对比了英国和美国银行转账的速度问题，质疑美国银行转账为何如此缓慢。

• [nu11ptr] 表示速度更多是“感知速度”，例如编辑器的输入延迟，而非纯粹的计算速度，并指出这种感知对用户体验有直接影响。

补充讨论：
• [foxrider] 建议学习触摸打字以提高与计算机交互的效率，认为这是一种被低估的技能。
• [SatvikBeri] 指出人们常常低估速度的好处，尤其是当速度提升能改变整个工作流程时，例如更快的实验迭代。
• [Aurornis] 认为速度一直是用户界面的优先事项，无论公司规模大小，用户对产品响应速度和页面加载速度都有很高的期望。
• [calibas] 强调高效代码不仅提升速度，还具有环保意义，因为高效代码消耗更少的电力并减少硬件升级需求。
• [betterhealth12] 仅提及Linear和JIRA的对比，未展开详细讨论。
• [chamomeal] 对比了过去和现在的游戏输入延迟问题，表达了对现代游戏响应速度下降的不满。
• [Night_Thastus] 抱怨现代开发环境中的速度问题，如C++编译时间和工具启动速度，表达了对更高效开发环境的渴望。

争议焦点：
• 速度是否总是软件开发中的重要需求，尤其是在用户不明确提出的情况下。
• 自动化工具和手动优化的效率对比，以及在实际应用中如何平衡这两者。

44736967.article_content:
fast
Rarely in software does anyone ask for “fast.” We ask for features, we ask for volume discounts, we ask for the next data integration. We never think to ask for fast.
But software that's fast changes behavior.
Developers ship more often when code deploys in seconds (or milliseconds) instead of minutes.
AI code complete means we can prototype in languages we're less familiar with.
Real-time streaming makes remote work possible.
Conversely, slow software limits us more than we realize. When was the last time you used airplane WiFi and actually got a lot done? Maybe you sent a few Slack messages or answered a couple emails. Google Docs worked half of the time. You probably gave up. Instagram usually works pretty well—Facebook knows how important it is to be fast.
Fast is magical.
Fast eliminates cognitive friction. Raycast surfacing the right application before you finish typing feels like an extension of your mind. Superhuman's
sub-100ms
rule—plus their focus on keyboard shortcuts—changed the email game in a way that no one's been able to replicate, let alone beat. I recently used Mercury to pay another business that uses Mercury, and its instant settle felt surprising in a world where bank transfers usually take days.
No one praises these tools explicitly for their speed. They just feel magical.
Fast signals simplicity
, which is even rarer in a world where code and content are commodities.
Fast software has nowhere to hide. Network calls and dependencies reveal themselves through latency, and this brutal honesty forces discipline. Companies that do fast very well tend to have very focused products.
This is because the effort to make software fast often requires stripping away non-essential features. Compare how fast a streamlined project management tool like Linear loads versus an enterprise app like Workday (or worse… Oracle). In a world obsessed with adding rather than refining, speed becomes the ultimate expression of respect. It says, "We've thought deeply about what matters and eliminated everything else."
In order to make things fast, you often have to do complex things behind the scenes. At Cash App, we were very careful to only introduce additional steps in the user's journey when it was absolutely needed, which meant we had to handle a lot of messiness in the background. In
this interview
, Kevin Systrom explains how Instagram
optimistically uploaded
users' photos while they entered their caption to make the upload experience feel instant. Fast isn't just a technical accomplishment—it signals prioritization and focus.
Fast is fun
Also, we like fast because it's fun! We count WPM typing speeds for very little benefit except that it's fun to be faster than other people. The first thing we do on a new computer is set-up our hotkeys so we can go at the same speed as our last set-up.
Fast is relative
A lot of LLM-augmented workflows are infinitely faster than their pre-LLM counterparts today. Asking an LLM to research for 6 minutes is already 10000x faster than asking for a report that used to take days.
And yet, it's obvious to anyone that writes code that we're very far from the standards that we're used to from the previous software era. We're very focused on capabilities, and we're not very focused on performance or experience. We accept the clunkiness because the magic is still new, and that's ok! It's all still way faster than a human. But the current tools we have to build, run, and deploy AI apps feel very far off from the developer experience that we'll have in the future. We haven't yet begun the phase where optimization becomes the priority.
When we do, you'll see more and more companies optimizing for low latency, interface design, connectivity, and reliability.
This
, in turn, will unlock new capabilities and use cases that we aren't yet even thinking about. After all, the best software changes the way we live our lives, and we build our lives around software that feels like superpowers.
==
Some other pieces about fast that I've liked:
Patrick Collison
,
Charlie Marsh
,
Paul Graham
.
april 9, 2025
← back

data.author: MattSayar
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了如何在减肥后有效保持体重，强调维持体重也是一项需要技巧的挑战。文章介绍了几个关键概念：

1. **总每日能量消耗（TDEE）**：包括基础代谢率（BMR）、食物热效应（TEF）、运动活动生热（EAT）和非运动活动生热（NEAT）。这些因素共同决定了每天燃烧的卡路里数。

2. **代谢适应**：指减重过程中BMR的下降幅度超过预期。

3. **自适应生热**：指减重期间总能量消耗的减少，包括BMR的降低和身体活动的减少。

文章建议，缓慢而稳定地减重可以减少BMR的下降。即使出现代谢适应，这种变化也不是永久性的，也不会显著影响长期体重维持。关键在于不过度节食，并给予身体时间在新体重上稳定下来。文章还提到了一种叫做“动态维持”的策略，以防止体重反弹。

How to Maintain Weight Loss
Have you found yourself struggling more with maintaining your weight than losing it in the first place? You’re not alone, and this article shares a few tips to help make it easier.
by
Leigh Peele
•
July 16, 2025
•
Articles
When people hit their weight loss goals, it’s easy to assume the hardest part is behind them. However, maintaining that progress is a skill with its own set of challenges. In fact, sometimes, people are more prepared for the initial grind of weight loss than for the long-term effort required for maintenance.
This article aims to provide a collection of skills to manage maintenance more effectively while hopefully making it feel sustainable.
Let’s dig in!
1. Really understanding the role of your energy expenditure
Let’s start off by looking at possible changes in your total daily energy expenditure and BMR during the course of your weight loss.
As a reminder, your Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) is the number of Calories your body uses in a day to do anything and everything: breathe, move, heal, think, run, sit, lift, etc.
Calorie targets are personalized based on your energy use and the rate at which you want to lose or gain weight. For a deeper dive, read
this article
. In summary, your daily energy expenditure comes from four main components:
Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR):
The energy your body needs to function at rest.
Thermic Effect of Feeding (TEF):
The Calories burned digesting and processing food.
Exercise Activity Thermogenesis (EAT):
The Calories burned during exercise.
Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis (NEAT):
The Calories burned through non-exercise activities like walking or fidgeting.
These factors determine how many Calories you burn daily, with each contributing a specific percentage to your total energy expenditure.
To add a little more clarity to this conversation, definitional views of metabolic adaptation (as discussed in
this article
) and adaptive thermogenesis are also relevant.
Metabolic adaptation
: A drop in BMR that’s greater than what you’d expect just from changes in lean body mass.
Adaptive thermogenesis
: A more inclusive term that refers to any decrease in total energy expenditure that happens during weight loss. While it can include BMR reductions, it can also encompass factors such as reduced physical activity or other energy conservation measures during a deficit.
For more details on this, check out
Greg’s article
on what happens to BMR after weight loss.
If you’ve been using MacroFactor to lose weight, then you know that your TDEE can fluctuate. These fluctuations over the shorter term are usually due to NEAT and EAT (which I’ll cover more in the next section).
TEF
probably won’t shift TDEE all that dramatically, but it’s worth a little consideration. TEF accounts for the Calories you burn when digesting food and will generally scale with total food intake. This means that if you increase your Calories during maintenance, you
could
see a slight increase in TEF. That said, keep in mind the overall composition of the food. For example, suppose you were eating low-Calorie and high-density foods (e.g., lean protein, vegetables, fruits) during your Calorie-deficient period, but then shift back to ultra-processed “fun” foods, you could lose the small TEF boost you got from whole foods. With all this said, it’s a pretty small swing either way, but since we’re diving in, it’s something to consider.
This moves us to your BMR (and, at times, metabolic adaptation). If you haven’t lost a lot of physical weight, then you probably don’t need to give much thought to alterations in BMR or metabolic adaptation.
If you’re losing a modest amount of weight, say, less than 10% of your starting body weight (and you’re taking a relatively slow and steady approach), the drop in BMR due to metabolic adaptation tends to be mild,
usually in the range of 5%
. However, if you’re dieting more intensely or losing a significant amount of body weight, adaptation tends to occur more quickly, and
BMR reductions of around 10%
can become more common.
That said, even if your BMR takes a slight hit during weight loss, most of that drop is simply your body doing less work to support a smaller frame. And while metabolic adaptation is real, it’s not
necessarily permanent nor does it make a significant difference
.
In the long term, your body doesn’t seem to cling to some fixed “
set point
” that drags you back to your starting weight. There’s physiological pushback during weight loss (more hunger, less spontaneous movement, a slight metabolic decrease), but those effects don’t necessarily stick around forever. What matters more is how aggressive the diet was, how long you stayed on the diet, and whether you gave your body a chance to stabilize at the new weight. And FYI, if you are worried about aggressive weight rebound, I highly recommend reading about
dynamic maintenance
within MacroFactor.

data.article_summary: Tom Brady在文章中讨论了竞争对手在追求卓越中的重要性。他以自己参与的两个主要竞争对手为例：密歇根州立大学与俄亥俄州立大学的橄榄球对抗，以及他与佩顿·曼宁长达十五年的竞争。布雷迪强调，竞争对手不仅是比赛中的对手，更是推动自己突破身体、心理和情感极限的力量。竞争对手能激发专注和动力，帮助超越自我。他建议大家珍惜那些促使我们挑战自我、突破极限的对手，并将竞争对手视为一种礼物。尽管在社交媒体时代这种观点可能显得过时，布雷迪认为应将对手视为“敌人”，以激发最高水平的竞争和表现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同领域中的竞争与对手关系，包括体育、商业和社会，以及竞争对个人和社会的驱动作用。

不同观点：
• [lordnacho] 认为在美式足球中，四分卫（QBs）之间的所谓“对手关系”并不准确，因为他们从未在场上直接对决。相反，防守端的球员与QB之间的对决更为直接。
• [oumua_don17] 主张费德勒和纳达尔之间的网球 rivalry 是体育史上最伟大的对手关系，暗示这种直接竞争的特殊性。
• [dmvjs] 指出竞争推动进步，但并非所有竞争都以相同方式体现，不同情境下竞争的性质各异。
• [charlesabarnes] 强调竞争能激励个人设定目标并自我提升，但将对手视为“敌人”可能不适合所有人。
• [cadamsdotcom] 认为竞争在体育中因规则平等而产生良好结果，但在商业中不平等的优势常导致垄断，而非良性竞争。
• [Animats] 将体育竞争与社会制度对比，认为缺乏竞争（如冷战时期的共产主义对资本主义）会导致制度腐败和社会问题。
• [xavdid] 提供具体案例，推荐纪录片《Rivals: Ohio State vs. Michigan》以了解体育中的对手关系如何促进表现提升。
• [hangonhn] 推荐电影《Rush》，展示了F1比赛中尼基·劳达和詹姆斯·亨特的竞争关系，强调戏剧化表现下的竞争主题。
• [CSMastermind] 分析了博客文章中的结构化写作方式，质疑是否存在一种常见的反思、学习和应用框架。
• [insane_dreamer] 反驳费德勒和纳达尔之间对手关系的观点，指出他们有着长期的友谊，表明对手关系不一定带有敌意。
• [reverendsteveii] 提出哲学性的思考，认为每个人都可以是自己最好的对手，自我提升不一定要依赖外部竞争。
• [darod] 简单表达了对汤姆·布雷迪相关帖子频繁出现的困惑。

补充讨论：
- 竞争的定义和性质在不同领域（体育、商业、社会）中的差异和作用。
- 对手关系是否必须带有敌意，或者是否可以建立在友谊和互相尊重的基础上。
- 自我竞争与外部竞争的相对重要性，以及个人如何通过设定内在目标来驱动自我提升。
- 竞争是否总能带来积极的结果，或者在某些情况下（如商业垄断）可能产生负面影响。

争议焦点：
- 在美式足球中，四分卫之间的对手关系是否合理，以及是否应将防守球员视为更直接的对手。
- 费德勒和纳达尔是否代表体育史上最伟大的对手关系，还是存在其他更值得注意的例子。
- 竞争是否需要外部对手，或者个人是否可以通过自我竞争实现同样的进步。

Every champion needs a rival
Published
9 days ago

min read
​
Read in Browser
​
July 21, 2025
Every week, I sit down to reflect on the events of the week, extract their lessons, and gameplan how to apply those lessons toward greatness and growth. It’s a system that has always worked for me, it can work for you too.
Welcome to The 199!
Sign up here
if this email was forwarded to you.
Every champion needs a rival
July is a slow month for sports in America, but over in Europe, where I was this past week for E1 Monaco with our
E1 electric boat racing team
, two epic matchups took place. Jannik Sinner vs. Carlos Alcaraz in the men’s final at Wimbledon, and Tadej Pogachar vs. Jonas Vingegaard at the Tour de France.
​
These elite athletes are the best in their respective sports, and they each have a chance to go down as the best to ever do it, thanks in no small part to the way they push each other. It got me thinking about
the power and importance of rivalry in the pursuit of greatness
and the gift that is high level competition.
REFLECTION
I had the privilege during my playing career to participate in two amazing rivalries.
First was Michigan-Ohio State, which goes back over 125 years and has produced so many legendary games.
At Michigan, we could lose every game but beat Ohio State and people would consider it a successful year
. Conversely, we could win every game and go to the Rose Bowl, but if we lost to Ohio State those same people might consider the season unsuccessful. That’s how much the rivalry meant to the folks in Ann Arbor.
​
Then there was my rivalry with Peyton Manning and the Indianapolis Colts, which developed over about fifteen years. From 2001 to 2015, we played each other every season but three. (In two of those three missed seasons our teams actually played but one of us was injured.) All told, my Pats teams won the regular season match-up and the overall head-to-head match-up, whiled around his teams won the AFC championship head-to-head match-up. Peyton won more regular season MVPs, but we won more Super Bowls. And over that whole time, we won a very similar number of games. Ours was a pretty even rivalry for a decade and a half—a rare thing.
LESSON
But rivalry is obviously more than just how many times you play someone. In its purest form,
rivalry is a uniquely intense kind of competition that challenges you physically, mentally, and emotionally
. It pushes you to confront your own limitations, and then it compels you to transcend them—to run faster, hit harder, throw farther, dig deeper—because in the end you know that the outcome of a rivalry matchup is going to mean more to you than if it were just another game.
And what I have found is that when you realize the magnitude of a rivalry’s importance—to you, to your teammates, to fans—it can either shut you down or it can unlock a new level of focus that you might otherwise struggle to reach, much less hold onto.
​
I knew, for example that when I played Peyton Manning, I had to be locked in all week and laser focused all game. I couldn't have a single bad play against him. I knew that one interception could cost me a game. I knew that game could cost me home field advantage. I knew that home field advantage could cost us a chance to go to the Super Bowl. That sounds like a hypothetical, but it’s the story of our week 8 match-up during the 2006 season, which they won. We both ended the season as division winners with identical 12-4 records, but the Colts got the higher seed, hosted the AFC championship game against us, and went on to win the Super Bowl.
This mindset isn’t unique to football. I’m confident that rivals in every other sport have similar stories. There’s just a level of focus, motivation and performance that only a certain group of people can get out of you.
APPLICATION
We should all have a deep appreciation for the rivals in our lives who push us past the point of comfort and force us to question the confidence we have in what we’re capable of. Because the challenge these fierce competitors present is the thing that will spur us to find within ourselves effective strategies to overcome our limitations and achieve new levels of success.
In this way, I think you have to look at great competitors and great rivalries as a gift.
But I also believe—and this is kind of an old school point of view considering where we are with social media these days—that you have to allow your rivals to become your enemies. True enemies, in your mind and on the field. You can, and should, respect them, but you can’t look at them like “friendly competition.” You have to recognize that they are trying to take what you are trying to earn. data.title: Critical vulnerability in AI coding platform Base44 allowing unauthorized access
data.author: waldopat
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了在大语言模型（LLM）革命背景下，代码生成领域发生的重大转变，尤其是“氛围编码”（vibe coding）的兴起。这种新方式让没有技术背景的用户也能通过自然语言提示生成全功能应用。平台如Loveable、Bolt和Base44引领了这一潮流，使用户能创建从个人工具到企业内部聊天机器人等各种应用。

Wiz Research在研究中发现，Base44平台存在一个严重漏洞，攻击者利用该漏洞可以通过提供简单的“app_id”值绕过认证，获取对私有企业应用及其敏感数据的完全访问权限。该漏洞在24小时内被修复，且未发现被滥用的证据。

文章强调，氛围编码平台的共享基础设施模式带来了安全风险，一个平台漏洞可能危及所有在其上构建的应用。研究旨在提醒业界关注此类AI开发平台的安全隐患，确保技术的安全演进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕应用程序安全漏洞及其暴露的问题展开的讨论，涉及安全漏洞的严重性、责任归属、技术与法律问题，以及对平台和品牌的评价。

不同观点：
• **[toddmorey] 和 [zamalek] 对安全漏洞的批评：** toddmorey 指出了一个非常简单的漏洞，通过提供非秘密的 app_id 就可以利用该漏洞，并对当前的安全状况表示担忧。zamalek 认为这种认证问题应被视为法律上的重大过失，尤其在“vibe-coded”授权方面，表达了对安全实践的强烈不满。

• **[sandeepkd] 对安全实践的分析：** 认为此类问题属于“安全通过隐匿”的典型案例，并指出许多应用都可能存在类似问题，反映出对当前安全设计模式的担忧。

• **[zahlman] 对平台名称的评论：** 对多个平台名称的独特性表示质疑，认为这些名称不太合适，带有调侃意味。

• **[darepublic] 对平台价值的质疑：** 认为这些平台只是将LLM（大型语言模型）包装了一下，本质上只是“胶水代码”，不值得过多的赞誉和关注。

• **[bgwalter] 提供的背景信息：** 提到多个平台创始人与 Unit 8200 的关系，并引用了 Wix 被用于创建虚假网站的例子，暗示这些技术可能被滥用。

• **[jus3sixty] 对整体行业问题的批评：** 认为无论是数据泄露还是其他问题，都不会阻止大公司的“利益列车”，因为有“风险管理”机制，暗示这种现象普遍且难以改变。

• **[bitwize] 对 GenAI 安全的调侃：** 讽刺地指出“GenAI”中的“S”代表“安全”，暗示当前生成式AI技术在安全性上的不足。

• **[swyx] 对平台间关系的调侃：** 戏称 Wiz 发现 Wix 的漏洞是“以色列对以色列的暴力”，带有幽默性质地指出多个平台之间的关联性。

• **[uponasmile] 对漏洞修复方式的质疑：** 质疑 Wix 是否手动修复了漏洞，还是利用 Base44 修复了它，表现出对平台技术能力的不信任。

• **[htrp] 对法律和合同责任的关注：** 关注 Wix 是否在合同中对 Base44 代码库的状态做出了保证，暗示可能存在的法律纠纷。

• **[oc1] 对黑客活动的预测：** 认为当前是黑客的“黄金时代”，无论是为了乐趣还是金钱，安全研究人员和脚本小子都会活跃起来。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：安全漏洞的严重性和责任问题。toddmorey 和 zamalek 强调了问题的严重性，而 sandeepkd 则分析了这种漏洞的普遍性和深层原因。
• 对平台的评价：从平台名称到平台价值，不同用户表达了不同看法，有的质疑其技术含量，有的则质疑其品牌名称的合理性。
• 对行业整体问题的反思：jus3sixty 和 bgwalter 提到了技术滥用和行业内难以改变的现象，反映了更广泛的行业问题。

Wiz

One of the most profoundly transformed domains in the wake of the LLM revolution has been code generation, especially the rise of vibe coding, where natural language prompts replace traditional programming. This shift has empowered millions of users with little to no technical background to build fully functional applications with ease.
Platforms like Loveable, Bolt, and Base44 are on the front of this movement - they have enabled the creation of millions of applications spanning from personal tools to enterprises that now rely on these platforms to build internal chatbots, create complex automations, and trust them with sensitive corporate data.
In
our mission to find novel AI and cloud risks
, Wiz Research has been looking into the security posture of these AI-powered development platforms to identify common vulnerabilities that may impact the industry as a whole – a mission that becomes even more important as these systems and technologies get infused into
governments and other critical infrastructure
.
Executive Summary
Wiz Research has identified a critical vulnerability affecting the popular
vibe coding
platform Base44 (
recently acquired by Wix
following an amazingly rapid rise) which allowed unauthorized access to private applications built by its users.
The vulnerability we discovered was remarkably simple to exploit - by providing only a non-secret app_id value to undocumented registration and email verification endpoints, an attacker could have created a verified account for private applications on their platform.
This effectively bypassed all given authentication controls that Base44 provided, including Single Sign-On (SSO), granting full access to what were intended to be private enterprise applications and the sensitive data they might have contained.
Upon discovering the vulnerability, we immediately and responsibly disclosed the issue to both Base44 and Wix who promptly validated our report. The vulnerability was fixed in less than 24 hours, with Wix confirming that there was no evidence of past abuse (see their statement below).
In this blog post, we will detail our discovery process and discuss how the security implications extend beyond the specific platform to the broader AI-powered development ecosystem.
Vibe Coding Platforms - Shared Infrastructure, Shared Risk
The term vibe coding was coined by OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy in February 2025 to describe a development approach where users fully trust AI to generate code without manual oversight. Platforms and vendors quickly emerged to offer this capability, democratizing software development by allowing anyone to build applications using plain language.
To grasp the severity of the vulnerability we found and similar ones, it’s essential to understand the shared-risk model of vibe coding platforms. All applications run on the vendor's shared infrastructure, meaning every customer inherits the vendor's security posture. This model introduces a critical single point of failure - a single flaw in the platform’s core, especially in a critical component like authentication, instantly jeopardizes every single application built upon it.
The rapid enterprise adoption of these platforms for critical functions - handling sensitive data through internal chatbots, automations, and business tools - is precisely why we decided to focus our research efforts on this emerging
attack surface
. By understanding the potential impact of these systemic risks and by working with vendors to address them, we can help ensure the secure evolution of this transformative technology, helping vendors become more proactive in their quest for security assurance.
Exposure Walkthrough
Our reconnaissance began by assessing Base44's publicly accessible domains. By mapping the external attack surface with straightforward reconnaissance techniques (passive and active discovery of subdomains), we identified around five internet facing subdomains. All appeared benign, hosting the main application, documentation, and marketing website - none of which initially suggested an interesting entry point.
Continuing with the research, we received an alert about two Swagger-UI interfaces that were publicly accessible across
app.base44.com
and
docs.base44.com
, providing information of internal documentation & API endpoints.
Swagger-UI is an open-source tool that provides an interactive interface for visualizing and testing APIs, making it easier to understand and interact with web services.
By leveraging Swagger's interface, we browsed through the API endpoints looking for any endpoint that might leak sensitive data, allow privileged permissions, or be accessible without authentication. The API documentation was well-organized into several segments, but one section immediately caught our attention: the "auth" APIs.

• **[darepublic] 对平台价值的质疑：** 认为这些平台只是将LLM（大型语言模型）包装了一下，本质上只是“胶水代码”，不值得过多的赞誉和关注。

• **[bgwalter] 提供的背景信息：** 提到多个平台创始人与 Unit 8200 的关系，并引用了 Wix 被用于创建虚假网站的例子，暗示这些技术可能被滥用。

• **[jus3sixty] 对整体行业问题的批评：** 认为无论是数据泄露还是其他问题，都不会阻止大公司的“利益列车”，因为有“风险管理”机制，暗示这种现象普遍且难以改变。

• **[bitwize] 对 GenAI 安全的调侃：** 讽刺地指出“GenAI”中的“S”代表“安全”，暗示当前生成式AI技术在安全性上的不足。

• **[swyx] 对平台间关系的调侃：** 戏称 Wiz 发现 Wix 的漏洞是“以色列对以色列的暴力”，带有幽默性质地指出多个平台之间的关联性。

• **[uponasmile] 对漏洞修复方式的质疑：** 质疑 Wix 是否手动修复了漏洞，还是利用 Base44 修复了它，表现出对平台技术能力的不信任。

• **[htrp] 对法律和合同责任的关注：** 关注 Wix 是否在合同中对 Base44 代码库的状态做出了保证，暗示可能存在的法律纠纷。

• **[oc1] 对黑客活动的预测：** 认为当前是黑客的“黄金时代”，无论是为了乐趣还是金钱，安全研究人员和脚本小子都会活跃起来。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：安全漏洞的严重性和责任问题。toddmorey 和 zamalek 强调了问题的严重性，而 sandeepkd 则分析了这种漏洞的普遍性和深层原因。
• 对平台的评价：从平台名称到平台价值，不同用户表达了不同看法，有的质疑其技术含量，有的则质疑其品牌名称的合理性。
• 对行业整体问题的反思：jus3sixty 和 bgwalter 提到了技术滥用和行业内难以改变的现象，反映了更广泛的行业问题。

Skip to content
Tuning Up
What’s Not to Like?
On similes, good and bad
By
Max Byrd
|
July 24, 2025
locket479/Flickr
Similes! I have hundreds of them on three-by-five notecards, highbrow and lowbrow, copied from newspapers, comic strips, sonnets, billboards, and fortune cookies. My desk overflows with them. They run down to the floor, trail across the room into the hallway. I have similes the way other houses have ants.
Why? To start, for the sheer laugh-out-loud pleasure of them. “His smile was as stiff as a frozen fish,” writes Raymond Chandler. “He vanished abruptly, like an eel going into the mud,” writes P. G. Wodehouse, the undoubted master of the form. Or Kingsley Amis’s probably first-hand description of a hangover: “He lay sprawled, too wicked to move, spewed up like a broken spider-crab on the tarry shingle of the morning.”
From time to time, I’ve tried to organize my collection, though mostly the task is, as the cliché nicely puts it, like herding cats. Still, a few categories come to mind. The Really Bad Simile, for instance. Examples of this pop up like blisters in contemporary “literary” fiction. Here is a woman eating a crème brûlée: “She crashed the spoon through the sugar like a boy falling through ice on a lake.” (Authors’ names omitted, per the Mercy Rule.) Or: “A slick of beer shaped like the Baltic Sea spilled on the table.” Sometimes they follow a verb like tin cans on a string: “The restraining pins tinkled to the floor like metal rain, hunks of hair tumbling across her face in feral waves.” Or sometimes they just make the page itself cringe and curl up at the corners: “Charlie’s heart rippled like a cloth spread across a wide table.”
Writing about sex can drive a writer to similes of unparalleled badness. Someone has borrowed my copy of
Lady Chatterley’s Lover,
but these more recent examples might do, from
The Literary Review’
s “Bad Sex in Fiction Award”: “Katsuro’s penis and testicles became one single mound that rolled around beneath the grip of her hand. Miyuki felt as though she was manipulating a small monkey that was curling up its paws.” Or this loving, if somewhat chiropractic moment: “her long neck, her swan’s neck … coiling like a serpent, like a serpent, coiling down on him.” Or finally (my eyes are closed as I type): “Her vaginal ratchet moved in concertina-like waves, slowly chugging my organ as a boa constrictor swallows its prey.”
Strange if not terrible similes can turn up anywhere. The 17th-century poet Abraham Cowley ungallantly compares his lover’s stubborn heart to a grenade that, as she enters a room, “will tear and blow up all within.” Famously but weirdly, T. S. Eliot’s unmedical Prufrock sees the evening “spread out against the sky / Like a patient etherized upon a table.” In the least romantic simile ever worked into a love poem, John Donne likens himself and his lover to a geometer’s “stiff twin compasses”: “Thy soul, the fixed foot, makes no show / To move, but doth, if the other do.” And he takes another stanza to say that the fixed compass leans toward the far one, “And grows erect, as that comes home.” This is the style of writing that Dr. Johnson called, somewhat scornfully, “metaphysical poetry”: “The most heterogeneous ideas are yoked together by violence.” (You might say the same thing about Wodehouse—man, eel in the mud—but he is being funny, not witty.)
Donne’s simile belongs to another category as well, the epic or Homeric simile. Every reader of the
Iliad
knows something like this picture of an attacking army as a wildfire:
“As when the obliterating fire comes down on the timbered forest / and the roll of the wind carries it everywhere,” and so the Achaean host drives ahead for another five lines. Modern prose writers can also unscroll a simile at surprising length. John Updike dives right in: “The sea, slightly distended by my higher perspective, seems a misty old gentleman stretched at his ease in an immense armchair which has for arms the arms of this bay and for an antimacassar the freshly laundered sky. Sailboats float on his surface like idle and unrelated benevolent thoughts.” And one would not like to have been the beefy Duke of Bedford when Edmund Burke imagined how revolutionary mobs might regard him: “Like the print of the poor ox that we see in the shop windows at Charing Cross, alive as he is, and thinking no harm in the world, he is divided into rumps, and sirloins, and briskets, and into all sorts of pieces for roasting, boiling, and stewing.”
Strange if not terrible similes can turn up anywhere. The 17th-century poet Abraham Cowley ungallantly compares his lover’s stubborn heart to a grenade that, as she enters a room, “will tear and blow up all within.”

data.title: Words about Arrays and Tables
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了数组和表作为函数的概念，并探讨了多维数组和表的结构扩展。文章首先指出，数组是将一组数字映射到同质值的函数，与关联数组和结构体不同。传统数组在一维上操作，而表（如Nushell和Pandas中的）结合了数组和结构体的特性，允许通过字符串键和索引访问数据。

接着，文章详细分析了多维数组，特别是在APL类语言中的应用，说明这些数组可以看作是函数的嵌套，且每个深度的数组具有相同长度。通过函数的柯里化，二维数组可以表示为接受行并返回列函数的函数，这允许进行矩阵转置等操作。

文章还讨论了如何将这一概念扩展到任意维度，并解释了如何通过函数变换重新排列数组轴。最后，文章简要提及了像素结构的表示，进一步说明数组和函数的紧密联系。总的来说，文章提供了一种统一的视角来理解数组和表，并预示了可能的新的变体。

主要讨论点：数组与表（Arrays and Tables）在不同技术背景下的实现与应用

不同观点：
• **D4M的优势**：teleforce认为D4M（Dynamic Distributed Dimensional Data Model）通过结合电子表格、表、数据库和图形的概念，基于关联数组数学，提供了一种清新且数学上严谨的选择，尤其是在面对将所有功能都加到PostgreSQL或者整合不同系统的情况下。D4M避免了过度复杂化，类似于SQL的关系数据库概念，但基于新的数学基础。
  
• **多维数组的语言支持不足**：Animats指出，现代编程语言在多维数组支持上存在不足。例如，FORTRAN早就有多维数组，但C、Go和Rust等语言没有直接支持。多维数组的切片问题使得设计变得更加复杂，尤其是在需要支持多轴切片时。讨论最终陷入了细节争论，没有任何实际进展。

• **对标题和内容的批评**：zahlman认为要求写满2000字是无意义的，甚至标题过滤机制也是一个误导功能。如果只是“数组和表”作为标题会更好，带有字数要求的标题通常意味着低质量的投稿。

• **XSLT/XPath的例子**：mvc提到XSLT/XPath提供了一种多轴访问数据结构的方式，这可能对数组和表的多维操作有参考价值。

• **历史背景与FORTRAN的索引机制**：nyrikki提到通过去除类型限制，可以更好地理解FORTRAN的多维数组支持。IBM 704计算机的索引寄存器和位运算结合，为FORTRAN的多维数组提供了基础，这种概念与现代BI工具（如Tableau）的实现有一定的历史联系。

• **代数形状与数组结构**：mpweiher提供了一篇关于通过代数形状构建数组的论文，讨论了如何从代数角度理解数组结构，进一步探讨了数组的多维性和复杂性。

• **数组索引的价值**：galaxyLogic质疑使用非整数索引数组的意义。他认为，通过定义整数值的命名常量可以达到同样的效果，并提出整数索引已经足够。

• **数组索引的灵活性与性能问题**：kccqzy认为大多数编程语言在数组索引上的限制（如必须使用整数）导致程序员不得不使用更通用的哈希表，从而牺牲性能。他以Haskell为例，说明了如何通过更灵活的索引机制提高编程的表达能力。同时，kccqzy还探讨了数组的长度问题和类型签名，特别是对无限集合和代数操作的同构性进行了深入分析。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了多种技术，包括Lua的表（tables）、PostgreSQL的广泛应用、XSLT/XPath的多轴访问、FORTRAN的历史索引机制以及Haskell的灵活数组索引，展示了在数组和表的实现上有多种不同的思路和历史演变。
• 关于多维数组和切片操作的复杂性，特别是在现代语言中的支持不足，也成为了讨论的一个焦点，说明这一问题在实际应用中具有普遍性和挑战性。
• 代数角度的数组结构分析和数组索引的灵活性问题，揭示了在数组设计中存在的一些深层次的数学和性能考量。

2000 words about arrays and tables
THEY'RE JUST FUNCTIONS
I'm way too discombobulated from getting next month's release of
Logic for Programmers
ready, so I'm pulling a idea from the slush pile. Basically I wanted to come up with a mental model of arrays as a concept that explained APL-style multidimensional arrays and tables but also why there weren't multitables.
So, arrays. In all languages they are basically the same: they map a sequence of numbers (I'll use
1..N
)
1
to homogeneous values (values of a single type). This is in contrast to the other two foundational types, associative arrays (which map an arbitrary type to homogeneous values) and structs (which map a fixed set of keys to
heterogeneous
values). Arrays appear in PLs earlier than the other two, possibly because they have the simplest implementation and the most obvious application to scientific computing. The OG FORTRAN had arrays.
I'm interested in two structural extensions to arrays. The first, found in languages like nushell and frameworks like Pandas, is the
table
. Tables have string keys like a struct
and
indexes like an array. Each row is a struct, so you can get "all values in this column" or "all values for this row". They're heavily used in databases and data science.
The other extension is the
N-dimensional array
, mostly seen in APLs like Dyalog and J. Think of this like arrays-of-arrays(-of-arrays), except all arrays at the same depth have the same length. So
[[1,2,3],[4]]
is not a 2D array, but
[[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]
is. This means that N-arrays can be queried on any axis.

1-dimensional arrays
A one-dimensional array is a function over
1..N
for some N.
To be clear this is
math
functions, not programming functions. Programming functions take values of a type and perform computations on them. Math functions take values of a fixed set and return values of another set. So the array
[a, b, c, d]
can be represented by the function
(1 -> a ++ 2 -> b ++ 3 -> c ++ 4 -> d)
. Let's write the set of all four element character arrays as
1..4 -> char
.
1..4
is the function's
domain
.
The set of all character arrays is the empty array + the functions with domain
1..1
+ the functions with domain
1..2
+ ... Let's call this set
Array[Char]
. Our compilers can enforce that a type belongs to
Array[Char]
, but some operations care about the more specific type, like matrix multiplication. This is either checked with the runtime type or, in exotic enough languages, with static dependent types.
(This is actually how TLA+ does things: the basic collection types are functions and sets, and a function with domain 1..N is a sequence.)

A function that takes a row and a column and returns the value at that index, so it would look like

.
A function that takes a row and returns that column as an array, aka another function:
f(r: 1..3) -> g(c: 1..4) -> Int
.
2
Man, (2) looks a lot like
currying

(+) 6 10

(+) 6

new

f y = y + 6
, and then applies
f 10
to get 16. So
(+)

Int -> Int -> Int
: it's a function that takes an
Int

Int -> Int
.
3
Similarly, our 2D array can be represented as an array function that returns array functions: it has type
1..3 -> 1..4 -> Int
, meaning it takes a row index and returns
1..4 -> Int
, aka a single array.
(This differs from conventional array-of-arrays because it forces all of the subarrays to have the same domain, aka the same length. If we wanted to permit ragged arrays, we would instead have the type
1..3 -> Array[Int]
.)
Why is this useful? A couple of reasons. First of all, we can apply function transformations to arrays, like "
combinators
". For example, we can flip any function of type
a -> b -> c
into a function of type
b -> a -> c
. So given a function that takes rows and returns columns, we can produce one that takes columns and returns rows. That's just a matrix transposition!
Second, we can extend this to any number of dimensions: a three-dimensional array is one with type
1..M -> 1..N -> 1..O -> V

• **XSLT/XPath的例子**：mvc提到XSLT/XPath提供了一种多轴访问数据结构的方式，这可能对数组和表的多维操作有参考价值。

• **历史背景与FORTRAN的索引机制**：nyrikki提到通过去除类型限制，可以更好地理解FORTRAN的多维数组支持。IBM 704计算机的索引寄存器和位运算结合，为FORTRAN的多维数组提供了基础，这种概念与现代BI工具（如Tableau）的实现有一定的历史联系。

• **代数形状与数组结构**：mpweiher提供了一篇关于通过代数形状构建数组的论文，讨论了如何从代数角度理解数组结构，进一步探讨了数组的多维性和复杂性。

• **数组索引的价值**：galaxyLogic质疑使用非整数索引数组的意义。他认为，通过定义整数值的命名常量可以达到同样的效果，并提出整数索引已经足够。

• **数组索引的灵活性与性能问题**：kccqzy认为大多数编程语言在数组索引上的限制（如必须使用整数）导致程序员不得不使用更通用的哈希表，从而牺牲性能。他以Haskell为例，说明了如何通过更灵活的索引机制提高编程的表达能力。同时，kccqzy还探讨了数组的长度问题和类型签名，特别是对无限集合和代数操作的同构性进行了深入分析。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了多种技术，包括Lua的表（tables）、PostgreSQL的广泛应用、XSLT/XPath的多轴访问、FORTRAN的历史索引机制以及Haskell的灵活数组索引，展示了在数组和表的实现上有多种不同的思路和历史演变。
• 关于多维数组和切片操作的复杂性，特别是在现代语言中的支持不足，也成为了讨论的一个焦点，说明这一问题在实际应用中具有普遍性和挑战性。
• 代数角度的数组结构分析和数组索引的灵活性问题，揭示了在数组设计中存在的一些深层次的数学和性能考量。

主要讨论点：Frigade产品的概念、网站设计及技术实现

不同观点：

  ◦ [flippy_flops]：赞赏概念和营销视频，但对AI解决方案的成熟度有疑虑，希望看到更具体的使用场景演示（如在Survey Monkey上的应用）。

  ◦ [twoodfin]：建议将代理反馈整合到开发者产品反馈中，认为这对产品经理非常有价值。
  ◦ [lyime]：赞赏多角色邀请功能，认为设计巧妙。
  ◦ [j45]：对产品概念感兴趣，并建议加入用户会话点击/交互历史的功能。

• 对网站设计和性能的批评：
  ◦ [Rohitcss]：认为网站的登陆页面流程奇怪，质疑是否在本地运行。
  ◦ [superasn]：认为登陆页面设计不佳，导致浏览器卡顿和CPU占用过高。
  ◦ [moomoo11]：网站让笔记本风扇狂转，建议简化页面设计，直接展示价值主张。
  ◦ [lawlessone]：关心产品是否在本地运行。
  ◦ [saberience]：强烈不满现代企业网站的设计风格，认为滚动体验差，建议直接展示内容。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：
  ◦ 网站设计和性能问题：部分用户对Frigade的登陆页面设计和性能表现提出批评，尤其是滚动效果和CPU占用问题。
  ◦ 产品功能实现细节：用户对多角色邀请、数据泄露风险和本地运行等功能实现细节表示关注。

• 其他值得注意的讨论点：
  ◦ [tuesdaynight]：询问产品是否支持多语言使用。
  ◦ [skeeter2020]：对多角色邀请功能的具体实现方式表示疑问，尤其是当用户不使用邮箱时的情况。

总结来看，评论主要围绕Frigade的概念和实际应用展开，有用户对其创新性表示赞赏，但也对其技术实现和网站设计提出了改进建议。

data.title: Ultra-Rapid Vision in Birds
data.author: downboots
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过行为实验研究了三种小型鸣禽（蓝山雀、领雀和斑姬鹟）的视觉时间敏锐度。研究发现，这些鸟类能够分辨高达145赫兹的光暗交替周期，远超基于其体型和代谢率的预测，并且比其他脊椎动物及人类的最高分辨频率高出约50赫兹。这种快速视觉能力可能源于自然选择的压力，有助于它们在飞行中精准探测和追踪快速移动的物体。研究表明，快速视觉可能是许多生态相似的鸟类共有的特征，而不仅限于猛禽的锐利视觉。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：鸟类是否能够通过眼睛运动或其他快速运动来感知高于闪烁融合频率的闪烁光，以及它们对闪烁光的反应速度是否比人类快。

不同观点：
• modeless认为，即使闪烁频率高于人类视觉的闪烁融合阈值，鸟类仍可能通过使用眼睛运动或其他快速运动来区分闪烁光。具体来说，modeless指出，恒定光源在运动中会产生平滑的模糊，而闪烁光则会产生多个清晰的图像。然而，该评论也提到，目前似乎没有方法验证鸟类是否通过运动来区分闪烁光。

• yrcyrc支持modeless的观点，并补充了一个相关的观察，提到有说法称鸟类反应速度比人类快13倍，这在鸟群飞行中尤其有用，因为它们需要快速处理大量视觉信息。这暗示鸟类可能确实能够感知高于人类阈值的闪烁光。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否能验证鸟类通过运动或其他机制感知闪烁光。modeless质疑当前研究方法的局限性，而yrcyrc提供了一个可能的解释，即鸟类快速反应能力可能使它们在某些情况下能够感知到人类无法感知的闪烁。

• 两个评论都提到了鸟类感知能力的潜在差异，尤其是与人类视觉系统的对比，强调了鸟类在快速运动和反应方面的独特优势。

Abstract
Flying animals need to accurately detect, identify and track fast-moving objects and these behavioral requirements are likely to strongly select for abilities to resolve visual detail in time. However, evidence of highly elevated temporal acuity relative to non-flying animals has so far been confined to insects while it has been missing in birds. With behavioral experiments on three wild passerine species, blue tits, collared and pied flycatchers, we demonstrate temporal acuities of vision far exceeding predictions based on the sizes and metabolic rates of these birds. This implies a history of strong natural selection on temporal resolution. These birds can resolve alternating light-dark cycles at up to 145 Hz (average: 129, 127 and 137, respectively), which is ca. 50 Hz over the highest frequency shown in any other vertebrate. We argue that rapid vision should confer a selective advantage in many bird species that are ecologically similar to the three species examined in our study. Thus, rapid vision may be a more typical avian trait than the famously sharp vision found in birds of prey.

data.title: Hexatetrahedral Rails
data.author: julik
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了软件开发中的六边形架构（Hexagonal Architecture）在Rails应用中的实践及其面临的挑战。作者指出，约十年前受领域驱动设计（DDD）和Alastair Cockburn的六边形架构启发，许多Rails项目采用了这种架构风格，但如今这些项目在升级和维护时遇到了复杂性问题。作者戏称这些项目为“hexatetrahedral Rails applications”，因为它们常常引入了超出预期好处的复杂性，甚至变成了不必要的“ complicationments”。

六边形架构的初衷是通过模块化和小接口组合实现解耦，但在Rails中实施时，往往导致不必要的间接层和维护负担。作者质疑这种解耦的必要性，尤其当应用的主要交付方式是Web时。除非应用需要嵌入到其他程序中，否则过度解耦可能弊大于利。作者建议从过去的实践中提取有价值的经验，而非盲目追随时尚。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rails中的数据操作、仓库模式（Repositories）的应用及其合理性、与框架解耦的必要性

不同观点：
• [pqdbr] 认为文章中关于 `user.log_entries` 在 Rails 7+ 中行为的说法不正确。根据其测试，`user.log_entries` 会如预期返回一个 `LogEntry` 实例，而不是文章所说的会返回空数组直到重新加载。
• [0x457] 认为仓库模式有其合理性。如果直接使用 ActiveRecord，那么无法责怪初级开发者在每次请求时对表进行全表扫描。同时，不理解为什么要替换 ActiveRecord 来创建仓库，而不是在其基础上构建。
• [static_void] 表示庆幸文章是讽刺和批评，因为只是出于猎奇心理点击进来。将其比喻为软件架构中的“看车祸现场”。
• [yakshaving_jgt] 支持与框架解耦的观点，并引用 Gary Bernhardt 的 Destroy All Software 视频系列作为支持。认为解耦、自定义持久层函数、通过自动化测试驱动设计都是好主意，并应避免昂贵的集成测试。
• [TOGoS] 对使用 `UsersRepository.find_all_with_email(...)` 的方式感到不解，认为如果要加载对象，应该从一个特定的仓库加载，而不是从一个类的仓库加载。同时指出，当应用需要从多个数据源获取数据时，数据与特定数据源的紧密耦合会造成混乱。这也是其不使用 Rails 的原因。
• [ryandv] 提供了一个历史背景链接，指向一篇在上次广泛讨论中标题具有挑衅性的文章，为讨论提供了更多的背景信息。
• [aaroninsf] 提供了一个关于类比的链接，为不熟悉文中类比的读者提供参考。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了 Rails 框架中的数据操作细节（如 `user.log_entries` 的行为）以及仓库模式的实际应用价值。
• 讨论了与框架解耦的必要性及其带来的好处，特别是在多数据源情况下。
• 引用了外部资源和历史背景信息，为讨论提供了更多的上下文和深度。

争议焦点：
• Rails 中数据操作的预期行为，特别是 `user.log_entries` 在不同版本中的表现。
• 仓库模式的应用是否合理，特别是在使用 ActiveRecord 的情况下。
• 与框架解耦的必要性和实现方式，特别是对于多数据源的应用场景。

44701001.article_content:
Software is a creative endeavor and a craft. And like any creative endeavor and any craft, it is subject to fashions. About a decade ago, one of those fashions was
Hexagonal Rails
largely inspired by the DDD book, but also by the original Hexagonal Architecture work by Dr. Cockburn.
Some of these applications are now up for their Rails upgrade and an “oil change,” and it’s interesting to see them in the wild and how they get perceived through the lens of the years that have gone by since then. I call them “hexatetrahedral Rails applications” - in jest, of course - because they often end up presenting complexities that go beyond the intended benefits, sometimes becoming what I’d describe as
complications
or even
complicationments.
And while I appreciate the good intentions behind this approach, I’ve found myself questioning whether the benefits outweigh the costs in most cases. So I felt that - at the very least - I want to suss out why it is valuable, but also - figure out how I define/detect those apps in the wild, and how to understand their
raison d’être
well. Not to be snarky - but to look for the nuggets of wisdom in there which can be useful for us, today.
Why the vitriol?
I use this term from time to time because I’ve observed teams struggling with the maintenance and evolution of applications architected this way. While most “adult” Rails codebases (anywhere from 7 to 18 years of age) tend to be messy, that mess usually is within the confines of the
knowable
and well-discovered Rails builtins - ActiveRecord, ERB, controllers, helpers, the works.
Hexatetrahedral apps, in contrast, present a different paradigm which is usually (not always) supplemented by a large amount of non-default tooling. That tooling also needs updating. It needs to be understood. It is often coming from a single person who might have either abandoned it, or decided to redo it nearly from scratch. The burden of maintaining those “divergent” dependencies is much higher than “just updating the Rails app.”
And all of that also comes with a lot of dogma, usually:
No, you shall not do a
User.where
directly, you have to do a
UsersRepository.find_all_with_email(...)
.
That setup often adds indirections that don’t necessarily improve the expressiveness of the codebase, while making changes more complex - because, for every change, the engineer needs to decide whether they will be dropping this “repository” or “domain design” approach and just hit the ActiveRecord subclasses directly - or keep up the approach of going through “the published pathways.”
The Original Premise
It is actually very instructive to try and understand the hexagonal architecture proposition – the original one. Alastair Cockburn, the author of the architecture, actually recently did a video presentation that is
worth a watch
– if you have touched a hexatetrahedral Rails application recently you will realize that this is not what the architecture implies.
The original premise is actually quite sound, and shares similarities with other well-regarded layering propositions such as “functional core, imperative shell” and is based on composition of modules over small interfaces. But to have the luxuries of that composition it is hardly necessary to subscribe to the entire bill of materials thought customary for a “Hexagonal Rails” setup.
Why It Kind Of Fails
And the arguments for doing a “hexagonal architecture” inside Rails quickly get thin. “Decouple from Rails”? Your app is a Rails app. Why would you want to “decouple” from Rails if the main delivery vehicle of your app is… the web and Rails? Ok, I did do one app that had even a modicum of success and that had CLI and web frontends, whereby in both the “meat” of the application was being exercised fully - that was
tracksperanto.
But other use cases are quite thin in the wild. A GUI version of your app? If you already have a Ruby runtime in place and you already need most of the dependencies - you can run a script that wraps a Rails Executor around most key mutating actions and you are good to go.
And that’s even mostly ignoring the fact that the prevalent majority of native GUI toolkit bindings for Ruby are abysmally bad and not getting better, except for calling Java UI libraries from jRuby. CLI for a point-of-sales terminal or something similar? You can let it talk to your application over what’s called a “driving adapter” in the terminology of Dr. Cockburn, but you don’t need to “decouple from Rails.” Most of the conversations I’ve had with people about this kind of boiled down to a circular argument, namely: “we need to decouple from Rails to be less coupled to Rails.”
Why
the said decoupling was so essential - I rarely could decipher.
Now, it is a very valid desire to have this decoupling if your deliverable is, in itself, a
library-like
thing that you want to make embeddable in other applications. But if that’s the goal - there are less rigid architectures which allow you the same. Make it a duo of two files (mod
44701001.article_summary:
文章讨论了软件开发中的六边形架构（Hexagonal Architecture）在Rails应用中的实践及其面临的挑战。作者指出，约十年前受领域驱动设计（DDD）和Alastair Cockburn的六边形架构启发，许多Rails项目采用了这种架构风格，但如今这些项目在升级和维护时遇到了复杂性问题。作者戏称这些项目为“hexatetrahedral Rails applications”，因为它们常常引入了超出预期好处的复杂性，甚至变成了不必要的“ complicationments”。

六边形架构的初衷是通过模块化和小接口组合实现解耦，但在Rails中实施时，往往导致不必要的间接层和维护负担。作者质疑这种解耦的必要性，尤其当应用的主要交付方式是Web时。除非应用需要嵌入到其他程序中，否则过度解耦可能弊大于利。作者建议从过去的实践中提取有价值的经验，而非盲目追随时尚。
44701001.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rails中的数据操作、仓库模式（Repositories）的应用及其合理性、与框架解耦的必要性

不同观点：
• [pqdbr] 认为文章中关于 `user.log_entries` 在 Rails 7+ 中行为的说法不正确。根据其测试，`user.log_entries` 会如预期返回一个 `LogEntry` 实例，而不是文章所说的会返回空数组直到重新加载。
• [0x457] 认为仓库模式有其合理性。如果直接使用 ActiveRecord，那么无法责怪初级开发者在每次请求时对表进行全表扫描。同时，不理解为什么要替换 ActiveRecord 来创建仓库，而不是在其基础上构建。
• [static_void] 表示庆幸文章是讽刺和批评，因为只是出于猎奇心理点击进来。将其比喻为软件架构中的“看车祸现场”。
• [yakshaving_jgt] 支持与框架解耦的观点，并引用 Gary Bernhardt 的 Destroy All Software 视频系列作为支持。认为解耦、自定义持久层函数、通过自动化测试驱动设计都是好主意，并应避免昂贵的集成测试。
• [TOGoS] 对使用 `UsersRepository.find_all_with_email(...)` 的方式感到不解，认为如果要加载对象，应该从一个特定的仓库加载，而不是从一个类的仓库加载。同时指出，当应用需要从多个数据源获取数据时，数据与特定数据源的紧密耦合会造成混乱。这也是其不使用 Rails 的原因。
• [ryandv] 提供了一个历史背景链接，指向一篇在上次广泛讨论中标题具有挑衅性的文章，为讨论提供了更多的背景信息。
• [aaroninsf] 提供了一个关于类比的链接，为不熟悉文中类比的读者提供参考。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了 Rails 框架中的数据操作细节（如 `user.log_entries` 的行为）以及仓库模式的实际应用价值。
• 讨论了与框架解耦的必要性及其带来的好处，特别是在多数据源情况下。
• 引用了外部资源和历史背景信息，为讨论提供了更多的上下文和深度。

争议焦点：
• Rails 中数据操作的预期行为，特别是 `user.log_entries` 在不同版本中的表现。
• 仓库模式的应用是否合理，特别是在使用 ActiveRecord 的情况下。
• 与框架解耦的必要性和实现方式，特别是对于多数据源的应用场景。

data.author: ycombiredd
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提到的是一个名为"gtrsnipe"的代码库，由用户"scottvr"创建并公开分享。目前，该项目有12个星标（Star），但还没有被其他用户复刻（Fork）。文章还指出，要更改通知设置，用户必须先登录自己的账户。文章内容简短，主要涉及项目的关注情况和基本的互动操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Github上一个音乐映射工具（gtrsnipe）的功能、应用及局限性

不同观点：
• **关注指法和和弦形状**：[omoikane] 对工具根据指伸距离评分表示关注，但指出工具没有考虑和弦形状问题，尤其是避免大横按和弦的需求，并建议加入对变调夹的支持。

• **工具转换应用**：[jarmitage] 提出该工具是否能将MIDI转换为http://strudel.cc的小型符号表示法，并提到之前的一个相关项目（midi_to_tidalcycles），暗示了对该工具扩展应用的兴趣。

• **工具的可靠性与重复段处理**：[robbomacrae] 对工具在处理乐谱重复段方面的能力表示关注，并提到自己在博士研究中类似的工具，强调了在处理乐谱相似性方面的挑战。

• **工具的局限性**：[nartho] 指出该工具仅限于6弦吉他和3种调弦方式，认为这限制了其在更广泛音乐类型中的应用。

• **支持与兴趣**：[jmkr] 对工具表示赞赏，特别是对ABC符号的支持，并表示有兴趣将其用于和弦图制作。

补充讨论：
• **其他类似工具**：[westurner] 提到其他类似工具如tayuya、Kord，并讨论了这些工具的功能和潜在应用，如LilyPond输出和文本界面创建。同时，还提到了与音效处理相关的工具和库，如pedalboard，暗示了对工具集成的可能性探讨。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于工具的功能局限性（如支持的弦数和调弦方式）以及在处理复杂乐谱（如重复段和特定和弦形状）方面的能力。这些争议反映出用户对工具扩展性和灵活性的期望。

data.title: Australia widens teen social media ban to YouTube, scraps exemption
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YouTube对未成年人账户的禁令及其影响

不同观点：
• WantonQuantum指出，该禁令仅针对账户持有，并不禁止16岁以下人群观看YouTube视频，因此影响有限。
• forgotoldacc认为，过去人们呼吁保护未成年人免受不良内容影响，而现在政府实施这些法律后，人们却感到困惑和愤怒，因为需要提交身份验证，这可能会导致更严重的隐私问题。
• simpaticoder建议，YouTube可以推出一个专门的教育平台，如education.youtube.com，以过滤内容，从而保留教育性内容，减少不适当内容的暴露。
• spicyusername认为，对10-12岁以下的儿童实施全面禁令是可以理解的，但对于年龄较大的儿童，全面禁止可能过于严厉，且执行上存在困难。
• m101提出，YouTube或许会推出没有YouTube Shorts的版本，因为Shorts可能使政府有理由进行投诉。
• seydor担心，这样的禁令会激化青少年对成年人的敌意，可能导致不良的社会后果。
• non-认为，青少年有能力绕过内容禁令，这样的措施只会促使他们更早接触到VPN等工具。
• SilverElfin质疑，为什么像澳大利亚、英国、欧盟等国家突然变得支持审查，这与他们作为自由民主国家的形象不符。
• like_any_other指出，应利用家长控制软件而非扩大国家监控，但政府在公众压力下选择了这一措施。
• 9rx讨论了YouTube作为视频分享平台与社交媒体的区别，认为两者在实际使用中已变得难以区分。
• asyx强调，YouTube对其职业生涯有重要帮助，尤其在学习方面，禁令将剥夺青少年获取丰富学习资源的途径。
• Jalad分享了个人经验，认为YouTube在教育方面非常有价值，但承认当前的人工智能和有毒内容环境与过去不同。
• ccppurcell反驳认为，YouTube上存在大量不当内容，且容易接触到，因此需要严格管理。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于如何平衡保护未成年人免受不良内容影响与保留教育性内容之间的关系。
• 另一个讨论点是执行此类禁令的可行性和潜在后果，包括隐私问题和对青少年心理的影响。
• 有人质疑这些措施是否会有效，或是否会导致更严重的问题，如青少年绕过禁令和隐私泄露。
• 对政府和科技公司在处理这些问题上的角色和责任存在不同看法。

data.title: Show HN: A high-altitude low-power flight computer for high-altitude balloons
data.author: mpkendall
data.article_summary: Tiny4FSK是一个旨在用于高空气球（HAB）的超小型高空追踪系统，目前处于研发和测试阶段。该项目使用1节AA电池供电，可持续工作10-17小时，采用4FSK调制和Horus Binary v2系统。主要硬件包括SAMD21G18A微控制器、Si4063传输模块、ATGM336H GPS模块、BME280环境传感器、TPS61200升压转换器和MCP1700降压转换器。代码采用模块化设计，支持扩展和自定义配置。天线系统使用70cm业余无线电频段（420-450 MHz），需要FCC颁发的业余无线电许可证，并配备优化的四分之一波长单极天线，以实现高效信号传输。项目文件和代码可在GitHub上获取，供爱好者和研究者使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高空气球（HAB）项目中的技术挑战和实现方案

不同观点：
• [paulgerhardt] 支持通过轻量级相机远程控制拍摄，但指出由于带宽限制（约30字节/分钟）和有效载荷限制（需低于100克），实现起来有难度。他建议拍摄后让气球回到信号友好区域再丢下存储卡。

• [normaldotcom] 提到自己曾参与HAB开发，并分享了以前开发的APRS追踪器项目，表示有意重启该项目。他还提供了相关项目链接，分享了FeatherHAB的设计和源代码。

• [dylan604] 分享了自己过去的HAB发射经验，尝试用Arduino和多个传感器构建飞行计算机，但由于内存有限和未预料到的GPS跟踪问题（45,000英尺以上民用GPS信号受限），项目遇到困难。他强调了与持证无线电操作员合作的重要性，并给出了实用建议（如不要忘记在气球上附上联系方式）。

• [Catbert59] 计划设计一个小型PCB用于气球项目，并提出了技术方案，包括使用2.4GHz LoRa进行高率遥测和433MHz低率遥测，选择STM32U系列芯片和ePeas的能量采集器，以应对极端天气条件。

• [guywithahat] 提到Sceye公司正在进行类似项目，并提供了招聘信息，但指出工作地点受限（需居住在新墨西哥州的沙漠中）。

• [prpl] 对其他评论者的项目经验表示不屑，使用了贬低性的语言（称其他人为"NEWBS"）。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是高空气球项目中的技术限制，特别是带宽和有效载荷的限制如何影响遥测和控制功能的设计。
• 另一个讨论点是气球发射中的实际问题，例如GPS信号的限制和发射前的准备工作（如附上联系信息）。
• 评论中还提到了多种技术方案的可能性，包括LoRa和WSPR等不同的遥测方法，以及使用特定芯片和能量采集器的设计思路。
• 最后，[prpl]的贬低性评论引发了一定的负面反应，但未形成深入讨论。

Tiny4FSK - The Lightweight Horus Binary Tracker Built for HABs
WORK IN PROGRESS
- Please do not rely on this as your only tracking system. Tiny4FSK is still in the R&D phase of development and testing.
NEW
- Incorporated new Rev. 4 PCB files and code (12/21/24).
STATE
- Rev. 4 is fully working! Currently testing.
What is the Tiny4FSK project?
Tiny4FSK aims to be an ultra-tiny high-altitude tracking system. It runs on 1 AA battery that lasts for 10-17 hours (a few seconds between position updates, can run longer if there's a longer delay). It runs on 4FSK (4-frequency shift keying), which means that it separates tones into 4 separate frequencies. Upon this, it uses the
Horus Binary v2
system, which is a relatively modern system popularly used with
RS41ng
.
What are High-Altitude Balloons?
High altitude balloons (HABs) allow space science enthusiasts to launch their own payloads to near-space (30km) at a cost of hundreds of dollars instead of millions of dollars.  This can be done for atmospheric research, breathtaking imagery, and scientific experimentation. While demanding meticulous planning, safety adherence, and technical skill in electronics and mechanics, this hobby rewards makers with a chance to get hands on with projects like electronic data loggers, camera systems, wireless communications, and more.
Parts and Materials
This codebase is meant to work with the Tiny4FSK PCB, also available on this GitHub repository. Key components include:
Microcontroller
-
SAMD21G18A
. A modern Cortex-M0+ microcontroller by Microchip.
TX Module
-
Si4063
. A transceiver from Silicon Labs, similar to the Si4032 on RS41 radiosondes.
GPS RX Module
-
ATGM336H
. A cheap, high-performance GPS module from ZHONGKEWEI.
Environmental Sensor
-
BME280
. A proven sensor from Bosch for measuring temperature, pressure, and humidity.
Boost Converter
-
TPS61200
. Boosts 1.5V battery level to 3.3V for the rest of the board from Texas Instruments.
LDO Step-Down
-
MCP1700
. A step-down converter from Microchip.
This list is not exhaustive. Additional components and passives are detailed in the schematic files.
The Codebase
This code is modular and separated into several different files for easy expansion. These files are listed below:
Tiny4FSK.ino
- Main Arduino file with control flow.
config.h
- Configuration file for user parameters.
crc_calc.cpp and crc_calc.h
- CRC16 generator files for parity bits.
horus_l2.cpp and horus_l2.h
- Horus layer 2 file, Golay error correction algorithm.
voltage.cpp and voltage.h
- Voltage detection using ADC values.
si4063.cpp and si4063.h
- Si4063 driver files for radio transmission.
4fsk_mod.cpp and 4fsk_mod.h
- 4FSK modulation functions.
delay_timer.cpp and delay_timer.h
- Low-level delay functions based on timers.
utils.cpp and utils.h
- A collection of utility functions.
Step by Step Setup Guide
Setting up the PCB
Carefully
snap off the USB breakout board from the board.
Solder on the female 1x4 header row onto the underside of the USB breakout. Solder on the 1x4 male header row to the corresponding adjecent pins (labeled VSS, GND, D-, and D+).
3. To program the board, attach the USB breakout board as shown in the photo.  Once the board is programmed, the USB breakout board can be removed for flight.
Antenna System
This system relies on the 70cm amateur radio band (420-450 MHz in the US), and requires an amateur radio license, issued by the FCC, to operate. A pre-cut braided copper
monopole
is included, optimized to transmit on this frequency. The included antenna is a quarter-wave monopole, meaning that the antenna is just a quarter of the wavelength of the signal, and yet it maintains a good SWR (quantification of how much signal is reflected back into the transmitter). There is a pad that supports a quarter-wave monopole, but also provides grounding pads for a coax connector if alternate antennas wish to be used.

44734983.article_summary: Tiny4FSK是一个旨在用于高空气球（HAB）的超小型高空追踪系统，目前处于研发和测试阶段。该项目使用1节AA电池供电，可持续工作10-17小时，采用4FSK调制和Horus Binary v2系统。主要硬件包括SAMD21G18A微控制器、Si4063传输模块、ATGM336H GPS模块、BME280环境传感器、TPS61200升压转换器和MCP1700降压转换器。代码采用模块化设计，支持扩展和自定义配置。天线系统使用70cm业余无线电频段（420-450 MHz），需要FCC颁发的业余无线电许可证，并配备优化的四分之一波长单极天线，以实现高效信号传输。项目文件和代码可在GitHub上获取，供爱好者和研究者使用。

data.author: gaws

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国部分州立监狱囚犯的生活条件，特别是在高温环境下缺乏空调设施的人道性问题。

不同观点：
• **观点一**（人道主义立场）：[kylecazar] 认为，将囚犯关在高温、没有空调的牢房中是不人道的。尤其在德州等高温地区，夏季气温极高，缺乏基本的生活条件如空调是不可接受的。虽然不要求达到像斯堪的纳维亚国家那样的高标准，但至少应该保证基本的人道条件。该观点引用了路透社的调查数据，指出在29个州中，近50%的州立监狱住房单元部分或完全没有空调，其中德州的情况最为严重，58个设施中有51个缺乏空调。

• **可能的反对方观点**（资源限制或惩罚立场）：虽然未在评论中直接出现，但可以推测出一种可能的反对方观点，即监狱系统的资源有限，无法为所有设施配备空调；或者认为囚犯因其犯罪行为失去了某些权利，包括享受舒适生活条件的权利。因此，即使条件较为艰苦，也可以被视为对他们的一种惩罚或威慑。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：评论中提到的主要争议在于如何界定“人道条件”的底线。一方认为即使在监狱中，囚犯的基本生活条件也应得到保障，特别是在极端气候条件下如德州的高温。另一方可能认为，囚犯的生活条件不需要达到一般社会的标准，艰苦的环境反而是刑罚的一部分。

• **数据支持**：[kylecazar] 引用了路透社的调查和德州刑事司法部门的数据，增强了对监狱设施中缺乏空调这一问题的关切，表明这并非个别现象，而是广泛存在于多个州，尤其是德州。

• **道德与现实的平衡**：讨论中隐含了对道德标准与现实资源限制的权衡问题。即使不要求达到北欧国家的高福利标准，基本的居住条件如空调是否应成为普遍标准，仍是一个值得进一步讨论的议题。

data.title: Evidence for hepatitis C virus involvement in bipolar disorder and schizophrenia
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了病毒感染与精神疾病（如精神分裂症（SCZ）和双相情感障碍（BPD））之间的关联，特别是通过研究脉络丛（CP）中的病毒RNA。研究使用来自Stanley Medical Research Institute的脑组织样本，对84例SCZ、73例BPD、23例重度抑郁症（MDD）和76例对照组进行了RNA测序。结果发现，SCZ和BPD患者的CP中更可能含有病毒序列，尤其是丙型肝炎病毒（HCV）。进一步分析显示，SCZ和BPD人群中的慢性HCV患病率显著高于MDD和对照组。尽管HCV未在 hippocampus 中发现，但其在CP中的存在与宿主转录变化相关，可能涉及先天免疫反应。这表明HCV感染可能与精神疾病的病理有关，而不仅是由静脉注射等行为引起。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HCV（丙型肝炎病毒）与精神疾病（如精神分裂症和双相情感障碍）之间的关联及其因果关系

不同观点：
• [_alternator_] 认为该研究揭示了HCV与精神疾病（如精神分裂症和双相情感障碍）之间的关联是真实的，但质疑HCV是否是这些疾病的因果因素。虽然HCV在脑部（脉络丛）中出现并可能引发局部免疫反应，但要得出“HCV导致精神分裂症和双相情感障碍”的结论仍存在较大跳跃。

• [hungmung] 提到治疗HCV的新药物可能引发躁狂发作，但目前尚不确定这种现象的具体原因。可能是药物本身导致，也可能是生活突然改变引发的反应，或者是由于身体不再需要对抗慢性感染而导致能量过剩，使人无法适应。

补充讨论：
• [_alternator_] 强调了研究中的机制性证据有限，目前仅知道HCV会出现在脑部并引发免疫反应，但这不足以证明HCV是精神疾病的原因。
• [hungmung] 提出了治疗HCV的药物可能带来的精神健康副作用，这表明在治疗HCV时需要考虑其对精神健康的潜在影响。

争议焦点：HCV是否是精神分裂症和双相情感障碍的因果因素，以及治疗HCV的药物对精神健康的影响机制。这两个问题目前都缺乏足够的证据支持明确的结论。

44737247.article_content:
Association of viral RNAs in the choroid plexus with bipolar disorder and schizophrenia and evidence for the hepatitis C virus involvement in neuropathology
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Bipolar disorder
Schizophrenia
Abstract
Many epidemiological studies have shown an association between infectious agents, particularly viruses, and psychiatric disorders including schizophrenia. However, evidence of a viral infection in the brain that associates with schizophrenia (SCZ), bipolar disorder (BPD), and major depression (MDD) has not been found. A potential reason for this discrepancy may be that viruses are more likely to infect the neuroepithelium than neural tissue. To test this hypothesis, we used viral sequence enrichment technology and performed RNA sequencing in postmortem choroid plexus (CP) isolated from 84 SCZ, 73 BPD, 23 MDD cases and 76 unaffected controls (CNT) from the Stanley Medical Research Institute brain collection. This approach enabled us to identify the presence of 13 viral species in the CP of 46 subjects. We discovered that CP samples collected from subjects with SCZ and BPD are more likely to contain viral sequences. In terms of individual viruses, the Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) was the only viral species that reached the threshold of statistical significance for an association with SCZ and BPD. Therefore, we focused on HCV to characterize the association between psychiatric disorders and viruses. Analysis of the TriNetX electronic health record database with data on 285 million patients revealed that the prevalence of chronic HCV was 3.6 and 3.9 percent in the SCZ and BPD populations respectively. The prevalence of chronic HCV in these populations was almost double that observed for MDD (1.8%) and approximately 7-fold higher than the control population (0.5%). These findings confirm previous studies that report higher HCV prevalence in SCZ and BPD and suggest that HCV infection may be associated with disease pathology rather than behaviors such as intravenous drug injection, since these behaviors are present in all three disorders. We analyzed hippocampus RNA sequencing data from the subjects identified to be HCV positive via sequence capture. We found that although the virus was absent in this tissue, HCV RNA in the CP was associated with consistent host transcriptional changes in the hippocampus that were potentially related to the innate immune response. Our results are consistent with previous studies and provide clues regarding the contribution of viruses to the pathology of psychiatric disorders.

data.title: Ferrari were SO impressed by the Xiaomi SU7, they bought one
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: 文章报道称，小米推出的SU7 Ultra电动车以其强劲的性能和加速表现引起了汽车行业的广泛关注，甚至吸引了超级跑车品牌法拉利的兴趣。据中国博主透露，法拉利购买了一辆SU7 Ultra，用于对其 upcoming电动车型平台的研发和 benchmarking（对标分析）。图片显示，这辆SU7 Ultra驶出了法拉利位于意大利马拉内罗的工厂。此外，还有消息称法拉利代表去年访问了小米总部，讨论联合开发下一代高性能电动机。SU7 Ultra拥有1,548马力，0-60英里加速不到2秒，最高时速超过200英里，售价却低于特斯拉Model S Plaid和保时捷Taycan Turbo GT，发布后迅速售罄。这一事件可能标志着汽车创新的领先地位正从西方转向东方。

主要讨论点：对小米产品及市场表现的评价

Jo Borrás
| Jul 29 2025 - 6:47 pm PT

With its
tire-blistering acceleration
and
record-setting performance
, the Xiaomi SU7 Ultra has been getting attention throughout the auto industry, impressing everyone who’s seen it. That “everyone” now seems to include the OG supercar brand, itself.
CarNewsChina
posted pictures from a Weibo user that reportedly show a Xiaomi SU7 Ultra exiting the storied Ferrari factory in Maranello, Italy. According to a Chinese blogger going by 西米露在博洛尼亚 (which seems to translate to “Sago Dessert in Bologna”), the prancing horse brand is actively benchmarking the Chinese hypercar for its own upcoming EV.
The SU7 Ultra was definitely coming from inside Ferrari’s facility. After verification, we learned this specific vehicle was officially purchased by Ferrari for testing, and the development of their next-generation electric platform.
西米露在博洛尼亚
Yet another Chinese auto blogger,
苏黎世贝勒爷
, claims that Ferrari representatives visited Xiaomi headquarters last year,
allegedly to discuss the joint development of next-generation high-performance EV motors
.
The Xiaomi SU7 Ultra made its debut last year
, promising 1,548 hp, sub 2.0-second 0-60 mph times, and a top speed well over 200 mph – all at a price lower than a Tesla Model S Plaid or
Porsche Taycan Turbo GT
. The car sold out almost immediately after it was unveiled, racking up some 50,000 orders almost overnight.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The new electric benchmark
Xiaomi SU7 Ultra at Fiorano; via Weibo user Piniluoshan.
In the automotive world, “
benchmarking
” is a process in which car companies systematically tear down each others’ competitive products to compare everything from sound insulation, vehicle ride and handling, component materials, and even manufacturing methods against their own or against other industry leaders. The goal is to evaluate performance, cost, quality, and other key metrics, effectively figuring out “where they stand” in the market.
If Ferrari really
did
buy an SU7 to benchmark it against their own upcoming electric supercar, it’s more than just a curiosity –
it could mean that the highest tiers of automotive innovation have shifted from West to East
. Maybe forever.

data.title: Silicon Is Coming to Smartphone Batteries for a Big Energy Boost
data.author: defrost
data.article_summary: Enovix公司开发了一种采用硅负极的新型电池AI-1，其能量密度比当前主流智能手机电池高出约20%。这一突破有望大幅提升智能手机的电池续航能力。硅材料的应用使得电池可以在相同体积下储存更多能量，为消费电子产品带来显著的性能提升。这一技术进步对于智能手机及其他便携设备具有重要意义。文章由IEEE Spectrum的撰稿编辑Charles Q. Choi撰写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple Vision Pro电池技术的未来发展及其市场潜力

不同观点：
• kridsdale3认为，通过改进电池技术，未来的Apple Vision Pro电池包可以缩小至现有尺寸的1/3（可能不需要使用腰包），或者在现有功耗水平下续航时间延长3倍。他还提到，传闻下一代Vision Pro将采用M4级别的芯片，进一步降低功耗。因此，kridsdale3预测，经过1到2次迭代，Apple可能会推出一款更具大众市场吸引力的产品。

• malchow则关注电池技术的具体材料改进，指出新电池技术使用100%活性硅材料作为阳极，而非仅在石墨中掺杂5%的硅。他还分享了一个展示生产过程的预览视频链接，对技术的先进性表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• kridsdale3的观点更侧重于Apple Vision Pro整体产品的市场潜力和用户体验的改进，特别是重量、热量和续航时间等方面。
• malchow的观点则聚焦于电池技术本身的创新，特别是材料科学方面的突破，如100%活性硅材料在阳极中的应用。
• 争议的焦点可能在于技术的实际应用和市场化时间。kridsdale3更乐观地预计短期内可以看到改进产品，而malchow则关注技术的实际生产和实现。
• malchow提供的视频链接为讨论增添了技术细节和可视化信息，使讨论更加具体和生动。

总结来看，评论主要围绕Apple Vision Pro电池技术的未来发展，讨论了电池体积和续航时间的改进潜力，以及新材料和生产工艺的创新。同时，也对技术实现和市场化的前景存在一定乐观但有区别的预期。

Every week, I sit down to reflect on the events of the week, extract their lessons, and gameplan how to apply those lessons toward greatness and growth. It’s a system that has always worked for me, it can work for you too.
Welcome to The 199!
Sign up here

Your actions reflect your priorities
It’s been more than a week since Scottie Scheffler won The Open at Royal Portrush. Yet he is still doing interviews about
an answer he gave
during Media Day, in response to this question: "What would be the longest you've ever celebrated something?"
His answer was basically ‘not very long.’ For Scottie, celebrations have been fleeting, in part because golf doesn’t fulfill the “deepest desires of his heart.” The golf course, he said, is not where he goes to find satisfaction. So “what’s the point?” (That was the line that went most viral.)
When I heard this, some of it resonated with me, because I had a similar experience around his age. But I also understood that what I was hearing was a young athlete trying to make sense of success without the benefit of the perspective that comes with years of experience.
In this week’s newsletter, I want to give you some personal insight from my own experiences that I think will help explain where true personal satisfaction comes from—it comes from
many
places, not just one—and how you create it every day, win or lose, by the way you show up in each part of your life.
REFLECTION
In 2005,
I gave an interview to “60 Minutes”
where I sounded a little bit like Scottie Scheffler. I’d won three Super Bowls in my first four years as a starter, and I was explaining to the interviewer how, when I looked at my trophies and Super Bowl rings, I found myself thinking, “there’s gotta be more than this…this can’t be all…”
​
I was 27 years old. I was young. My first son, Jack, wouldn’t be born for another year-and-a-half. Football was a very important part of my life. But similar to Scottie, I could feel myself resisting the expectation placed on elite athletes, by the media and by society in general, to use professional achievement as the primary meter for personal satisfaction.
“What else is there for me?” I asked myself during that interview.
“What’s the answer?” the interviewer wondered.
“I wish I knew,” I said.
I would figure it out, but it took time. The lessons came in stages. First, that there is more to life than playing football and winning championships. Then I learned exactly what those other things were. Then, I learned how they all fit together so that what I did on the field supported the things I did off the field, and vice versa. And finally,
most importantly,
I learned that it was the pursuit of excellence in each of these areas where I found the most joy, not in the achievements themselves. It was the process, not the outcome.
I’m 25 years removed from the beginning of my pro football career, and a lot has changed since that interview. I have three kids now. I’ve played for two teams. I’ve started companies, invested in start-ups, taken ownership stakes in teams in multiple sports. I have teammates
and
employees now. I’m a broadcaster. I am a spokesperson, a business partner, a father, a friend and a brother and a son. I’m a decent golfer and a good leader. I have deep ties to both my local community and the global community.
Like most people, I have a lot going on. I don’t just do one thing. I do many things, though not all at the same time. I can’t. No one can—at least not if they want to be great at as many things as possible without sacrificing the satisfaction that can be derived from pursuing all the other things they care about.
LESSON
We all have different parts of our lives. You can think of them like a pyramid. At the top is yourself, and your physical, mental, and emotional health. Then there’s the relationship with your significant other or partner. Then you have your children, then your work, then your extended family, your friends, your hobbies, and finally your greater community.
​
Every layer of that pyramid is a priority. At any given moment, one of these priorities is taking precedence over the others. And the question is always whether it’s the right priority for the moment. That is the question it seems Scottie Scheffler is wrestling with: do I have my priorities straight? But I think figuring out that answer is fairly straightforward. When the priority is to take care of your mental and physical health, which is #1 always, that’s what you do. First you take care of yourself, then your partner, then your kids, and so on. When the priority is to take care of your career, whether it’s a three-week training camp or four rounds of major cham

• darod的评论引发了对社交媒体算法或内容推荐系统的质疑，暗示平台可能没有很好地反映用户的实际兴趣或优先事项。
