data.title: A short post on short trains
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：地铁系统的列车长度、车站设计和运营效率之间的权衡

不同观点：
• **支持小列车和小车站的观点**：小列车和小车站可以降低建设成本，并且通过增加列车频次来弥补运力不足。这种设计在新建地铁系统时具有经济优势，特别是在预算有限或城市空间受限的情况下。然而，这种设计的风险在于一旦需求超出预期，系统的扩容将非常困难和昂贵。
  
• **反对小列车和小车站的观点**：小列车在高峰期容易导致拥堵，乘客需要等待多趟列车才能上车。此外，小列车在信号系统和维护方面可能带来更高的运营成本。例如，慕尼黑的地铁系统虽然通过缩短列车间隔提高了频次，但在高峰期仍然出现过度拥挤和延误的问题。

• **关于等待时间和总出行时间的观点**：等待时间是影响公共交通效率的重要因素，特别是在列车间隔较长的情况下，实际出行时间会比预期长很多。即使在拥有优秀公共交通系统的城市，不确定的等待时间和不可靠的班次也会影响出行体验。

• **创新方案的讨论**：有评论提出短列车但长站台的方案，通过将站台分为多个登车区，让列车不必等待前车离开即可进站，从而提高频次。还有评论建议通过不同服务模式的组合，让列车跳站运行以提高速度和效率。

补充讨论：
• **自动化和运营成本**：自动化和无人驾驶列车被认为是降低运营成本的一个重要手段，尤其是在减少人力成本方面。然而，自动化系统也需要考虑信号系统的复杂性和维护成本。

• **长期规划和扩容问题**：有评论指出，虽然初期建设长站台和短列车的成本较低，但如果需求增长超过预期，扩容将面临巨大的技术和经济挑战。相比之下，初期建设更长的站台和列车可能在长远来看更具经济性。

• **实际案例的参考**：一些评论提到了新加坡的环线和慕尼黑的地铁系统作为小列车系统的例子，指出了这些系统在高峰期的局限性。此外，有人提到哈德逊-伯根轻轨作为近期建造的例子，认为其符合多项小列车系统的特点。

• **其他创新概念**：包括 rollercoaster 管道系统和 Turing 机器头站台设计等，虽然这些概念较为理论化，但也为地铁系统的设计提供了新的思路。

争议焦点：小列车和小车站设计在初期建设中的经济优势与未来扩容难度之间的权衡是主要争议点。支持者认为初期成本低且灵活，反对者则担心高峰期拥堵和扩容困难。

data.author: akkartik
data.article_summary: 《Fantasy & Science Fiction》v004n06是1953年6月的科幻与奇幻杂志，属于英文的经典纸浆杂志系列。该期包含多种类型的科幻和奇幻故事，代表了1950年代早期的科幻文学。杂志大小为223.5M，由Internet Archive Python库1.0.10版本扫描上传。用户可以下载多种格式如EPUB、PDF、HOCR等，适合不同阅读需求。该杂志在2017年5月1日由The Pulp Librarian上传至网络存档，包含用户评论和较高的阅读量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一篇包含"Bach beetle"概念的科幻故事的各种联想和延伸讨论

不同观点：
• [ggm] 认为 Bach beetle 的行动会有特定的模式，但这种模式是复杂的、看似无序的，甚至可能是分形的。这暗示了故事中可能包含的科学或数学元素。
• [Jtsummers] 提供了故事的直接链接，为其他讨论者提供了查阅原始文本的便利，但并未对故事内容发表具体看法。
• [Terr_] 提出了一种科幻设想，将歌曲《It's A Small World After All》的歌词嵌入耐辐射奇球菌的基因组中，并提供了一个相关研究的链接。这一观点扩展了故事中可能涉及的生物科技和数据存储的讨论。
• [zabzonk] 认为该作品并非 Philip K. Dick 的最佳作品，但指出该期杂志中有多位著名通俗文学作家，这可能是对该期杂志整体质量的评价。
• [stronglikedan] 建议故事中应使用鸟类，并提供了一个视频链接来支持其观点，可能是认为鸟类的行为或象征意义更适合故事的主题。
• [readthenotes1] 指出了故事《Ants》的作者与创造罗杰·摩尔饰演的圣人的角色之间的关系，这可能是对作者创作背景的补充。

补充讨论：

data.title: Emacs: The macOS Bug
data.author: xlii
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了Emacs在MacOS上的一个长期存在的性能问题，即随着使用时间的增加，Emacs的RAM占用不断上升，最终导致冻结。尽管在Linux和Windows上没有类似问题，作者发现MacOS上的Emacs在处理事件时会频繁分配和释放资源，尤其是在高DPI显示器下，这导致大量无用的缓存对象累积，从而影响性能。问题主要出现在`[NSApp run]`的调用上，它在处理系统事件时会无意中创建和销毁大量资源，如窗口、字体和图形上下文。由于MacOS高效处理事件的特性，这些问题在快速硬件上更加明显，最终导致Emacs无法正常释放资源，引发内存和CPU占用过高的问题。虽然问题复杂，但作者对代码设计并不持批评态度，而是理解其历史和维护难度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Emacs在不同平台（尤其是macOS）上的性能和兼容性问题

不同观点：
• **Emacs与GUI框架的主循环冲突**：[rayiner] 指出Emacs希望控制主循环，而大多数GUI框架也希望控制主循环，这种冲突导致了一些问题。不过，他在Mac上的使用体验一直很好，特别是处理大型PDF文件时表现优异。

• **macOS对Emacs的严格要求有助于改进跨平台代码**：[rahen] 认为macOS对Emacs中某些“hack”的严格处理有助于改进整个Emacs代码库，并提到PGTK前端和采用SDL工具包的潜力。

• **对改进工作的感谢和兴趣**：[dwb] 表达了对Emacs开发工作的兴趣和感谢，但表示没有时间和精力参与。

• **内存管理问题**：[kkylin] 发现删除一个帧（frame）时没有释放相关联的内存，导致长时间运行时内存消耗增加，并提出了一种临时解决办法。

• **在macOS上良好的使用体验**：[mattlangston] 提到在macOS上长时间使用Emacs处理大量缓冲区时，内存使用和性能表现良好。

• **对性能问题的不同体验**：[eviks] 提到Emacs在macOS上的性能问题早已被注意到，并解释了某些操作（如拖动窗口）可能导致大量内存分配和重新分配。

• **跨平台性能差异**：[vim-guru] 提到在Linux和macOS上没有发现性能问题，但在Windows上性能显著下降，甚至需要修改代码以使其正常构建。

• **线程和LSP问题**：[lygaret] 提到在macOS上遇到线程睡眠挂起的问题，导致LSP相关功能出现问题，并提供了一个补丁链接。

• **子进程导致的性能问题**：[bitwize] 提到在使用Emacs工作流（如magit）时，由于端点安全软件的激活导致性能下降。

• **非自由操作系统上的使用体验**：[hollerith] 认为在非自由操作系统（如macOS）上使用Emacs的困难可能是由一些Emacs维护者的态度导致的。

• **NS和w32线程模型的讨论**：[quotemstr] 建议在macOS上使用类似于Windows的独立线程模型，以解决主循环问题。

• **考虑放弃Emacs**：[algo_lover] 提到在macOS上使用Emacs时遇到性能和流畅性问题，正在考虑转向其他编辑器，如NeoVim或Helix。

• **使用Jemalloc改进内存管理**：[anthk] 建议使用Jemalloc来改进Emacs在macOS上的内存管理问题，并提到Lucid构建的可能优势。

• **倾向于在终端中使用Emacs**：[jrockway] 更喜欢在终端中使用Emacs，以避免窗口系统带来的问题，并提到在Linux和macOS上使用终端的经验。

补充讨论：
• **开发者对Emacs在不同平台上的性能和兼容性问题的关注和讨论**。
• **具体问题如内存管理、线程问题、GUI框架冲突等的技术细节和临时解决方案**。
• **不同用户在不同平台上的使用体验差异，以及对Emacs未来改进的期望**。

44737676.article_content:
home
2025-07-27
Emacs: The MacOS Bug
The Context
I have been recently roaming.
Doing some Zig, doing some Go, some Janet. Some C integration. Should have focused on my project but life threw more at me than I could handle, so I sought… happy distractions.
My experience with those technologies taught me new tricks and one day, when I needed some more distraction, I decided to debug something that had made me furious for years: Emacs jank
1
.
Whatever build I tried, whatever configuration I used, Emacs always rose in RAM usage. It became slower and slower within hours of use and eventually froze completely, requiring a kill.
I have read many complaints about performance searched for debugging techniques, possible causes etc. Some things helped others didn’t, but nothing made my experience closer to that on Linux or Windows.
All the sanctioned profiling I did hadn’t uncovered any anomalies. Crashdumps looked fine, sometimes showing that a hang happens on
ns_select_1
; something I wouldn’t expect to be a problem. Everything was reporting near-perfect behavior. Only thing that seemed off was CPU and MEM heavy
redisplay_internal
, but rendering big canvas on a HiDPI display might be costly.
Seemed to be “It’s not you, it’s me”. Until I got my hands on the traces.
Meta-consideration
Before going any further, I need to emphasize that, after spending more than a week digging into nsterm.m
2
, I’m not critical about the design or implementation
It’s easy to claim that something was badly designed or implemented inefficiently. Experience often points to simple reasons: growing complexity and lack of time.
In Emacs’ specific code case for MacOS, I could almost see how it developed over time and how layers upon layers were carefully layered, slowly tangling roots into a complex mesh. With the ever-changing MacOS API, maintaining the code likely took more effort than maintainers could provide. Besides,
it’s not a secret
that MacOS isn’t the primary platform - which explains the multiple flavors of Emacs on MacOS: Emacs Doom, MacPorts Emacs, Emacs Makefile, Homebrew distribution, Homebrew Emacs-Plus or Mitsuharu Yamamoto’s emacs-mac, to name a few.
Even though the bug exists on such a non-primary platform, the visible care of the code makes it easy to track. For me - and I’m not an expert in Objective-C, C or MacOS system engineering.
Issue
The problem is awkward as because it revolves around
[NSApp run]
3
invocations.
What this invocation does is it starts the main run loop, draining all pending event (the queue is shared) and then exits. It doesn’t seem to be problematic at all. Yet, it’s often used to process upcoming low-level system messages. Notably inside
ns_select
(replacement for
pselect
) and
ns_read_socket
, a communication pipe between “core” Emacs and GUI.
And inside it, there is barely visible side effect. Run invocation often occurs within
NSAutoreleasePool init
, which starts blank memory slate. Since it initiates a blank run, it creates everything that the main run loop would do during initialization: It creates windows, initializes graphical context, loads glyphs, fonts, and draws the frame.
It sounds horrible. But does it make sense? If it’s that bad - why didn’t anyone notice?
Because Emacs is very efficient.
This invocation is run as a response to an event - which can be almost anything. MacOS processes events rapidly in an async way. However, it’s also very efficient at juggling resources. Emacs, a pinnacle of engineering excellence, sets up and tears down resources in milliseconds.
…and the faster your hardware is, the faster it happens.
For instance, dragging a window handle - depending on the machine - could result in thousands if not millions of such events, causing allocation and reallocation of gigabytes of memory; Emacs is preparing you a new, laid-out window that is deallocated half a millisecond later because you’re not done yet.
Rapid allocations and deallocations cause various issues. Some allocations aren’t released. On purpose, because it’s the “core” Emacs which should handle closing, releasing resources, etc. However, if it didn’t expect those phantom instances, some small allocations might hang. NSMenu items, some strings, and glyphs could be affected. Emacs is unaware that
pselect
might be doing that, so it’s not cleaning them up.
Amusingly, when MacOS sees thousands of similar allocations, it starts to… cache them, “perceiving” them as important. They’re mostly useless: already loaded font glyphs in live windows, menu strings, copies of the current state of the rendered frame for use in the next re-rendering events. Those objects are allocated in hundreds of thousands, maybe millions. However, things like Emacs variables, search results reads, and counted in 100s are being pushed out further and further.
All of this processing is unbounded. The faster your Mac can process the events, the more loops happen. The higher DPI of your display - the bigger IOSurface size
4
and the bigger t
44737676.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了Emacs在MacOS上的一个长期存在的性能问题，即随着使用时间的增加，Emacs的RAM占用不断上升，最终导致冻结。尽管在Linux和Windows上没有类似问题，作者发现MacOS上的Emacs在处理事件时会频繁分配和释放资源，尤其是在高DPI显示器下，这导致大量无用的缓存对象累积，从而影响性能。问题主要出现在`[NSApp run]`的调用上，它在处理系统事件时会无意中创建和销毁大量资源，如窗口、字体和图形上下文。由于MacOS高效处理事件的特性，这些问题在快速硬件上更加明显，最终导致Emacs无法正常释放资源，引发内存和CPU占用过高的问题。虽然问题复杂，但作者对代码设计并不持批评态度，而是理解其历史和维护难度。

data.title: Traccar: an open source GPS tracking system
data.author: saikatsg
data.article_summary: Traccar是一个开源的GPS跟踪系统，包含基于Java的后端服务，支持超过200种GPS协议和2000多种GPS设备型号。它兼容主流SQL数据库，并提供REST API便于集成。Traccar解决方案包括网页应用、Android和iOS管理应用，以及用于跟踪移动设备的客户端应用。其功能包括实时GPS跟踪、驾驶行为监控、报告生成、地理围栏、报警通知、账户和设备管理，以及电子邮件和短信支持。项目遵循Apache-2.0许可证，由Anton Tananaev和Andrey Kunitsyn等人维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自托管系统的功能和可配置性

不同观点：
• precommunicator认为该自托管系统运行良好，能够追踪所有设备，并且可以连接到车内硬连线的GPS设备。他还提到该系统支持几乎无限的GPS设备和协议列表，具有高度的可配置性。他通过在车内添加蓝牙温度信标，并编写特定计算属性，成功将原始温度数据转换并保存，展示了系统的灵活性。
• cranberryturkey则对precommunicator的描述表示需要更多具体例子，暗示对系统的实际应用和配置细节缺乏直观的理解。

补充讨论：
• precommunicator通过个人经验提供了具体的使用场景，如追踪设备和车载GPS集成，并详细描述了如何通过计算属性处理温度数据，展示了系统的强大功能。
• cranberryturkey的评论反映了部分用户可能需要更详细的操作示例以理解和使用该系统。这表明尽管系统功能强大，但其复杂性和配置需求可能对某些用户构成挑战。
• 争议的焦点在于系统的易用性和用户对具体实例的需求。虽然precommunicator展示了其个人成功案例，但cranberryturkey则代表了那些需要更明确指导的用户群体。

Traccar
Overview
Traccar is an open source GPS tracking system. This repository contains Java-based back-end service. It supports more than 200 GPS protocols and more than 2000 models of GPS tracking devices. Traccar can be used with any major SQL database system. It also provides easy to use
REST API
.
Other parts of Traccar solution include:
Traccar web app
Traccar Manager Android app
Traccar Manager iOS app
There is also a set of mobile apps that you can use for tracking mobile devices:
Traccar Client Android app
Traccar Client iOS app
Features
Some of the available features include:
Real-time GPS tracking
Driver behaviour monitoring
Detailed and summary reports
Geofencing functionality
Alarms and notifications
Account and device management
Email and SMS support

data.title: The hype is the product
data.author: lr0
data.article_summary: 文章指出，大型上市科技公司不再专注于客户需求，而是更关心股东和股票价格。决策者往往通过股票期权或与股票表现挂钩的奖金获利，导致产品只需“勉强够好”来留住用户即可。垄断成为硅谷的核心商业模式，不同服务商之间缺乏互操作性，如Google Workspace和Microsoft 365之间的文件共享困难，这是商业决策而非技术限制。这种壁垒使得用户即便不满服务，也不愿迁移到其他平台，从而被持续剥削。公司利用炒作维持高股价，如Meta从元宇宙转向AI的策略，尽管曾因元宇宙损失巨额资金。科技公司通过制造 hype 推动股票上涨，而非改善产品服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科技公司是否因追逐短期利益和炒作而忽视客户体验，以及AI技术是否被过度炒作。

不同观点：
• johndhi认为，科技公司不一定需要垄断才能忽视客户体验，许多上市公司为了追求股价和投资者利益，会倾向于炒作而非专注于客户体验。同时，指出ChatGPT的成功在于其改善了搜索体验，表明长期忽视客户需求是错误策略。
• marcellus23反驳了反LLM（大型语言模型）的观点，认为这些工具并非毫无用处，虽然存在"幻觉"问题，但仍有部分文本生成与现实相关。批评将LLM视为无用的观点为卢德主义。
• ankit219对一项关于开发人员因使用AI工具而降低生产力的研究提出质疑，指出该研究存在多种限制条件，不能一概而论。
• mrweasel认为资本主义体系出现问题，导致产品质量下降但价格上升，并以特斯拉股票为例，说明其价格与公司实际表现无关，完全是炒作驱动。
• bagacrap将责任归咎于金融行业，认为科技公司只是对市场力量作出反应。以Meta为例，指出扎克伯格是在市场压力下才转向AI。
• pedalpete认为当前市场充满恐惧和贪婪，正处于炒作周期中，并引用市场杠杆趋势数据支持观点。
• micromacrofoot提出社会受"氛围"驱动，市场变得越来越不理性，谎言和负面情绪可以轻易影响市场价值。
• h2zizzle认为炒作是财富不平衡的产物，资本流入"愚蠢的婴儿潮事物"，并指出年轻人的意见因缺乏资本而被忽视，经济灾难可能是唯一能改变现状的途径。
• alsefj抱怨LinkedIn用AI替代传统工作搜索功能，导致用户体验下降，并决定删除账户。

补充讨论：
• 多个评论提到市场对科技公司决策的影响，尤其是股票和投资者对员工和产品决策的影响（murdockq, gowld）。
• 一些评论关注AI技术的潜力和实际效果，指出在批评其局限性时不应一概而论（ankit219, marcellus23）。
• 关于资本主义和市场动态的讨论反映了对当前经济体系的广泛担忧和批评（mrweasel, bagacrap, h2zizzle）。

争议焦点：
• 科技公司是否因追逐短期利益而忽视客户体验，以及AI技术是否被过度炒作并导致负面影响。

44737346.article_content:
Large publicly traded tech companies seem to no longer consider their
customers – that is, people and organizations who actually buy their
products or pay for access to their services – their core focus. The
focus has instead turned towards the stock price.
Their real clients, the entities they
really
care about, are
the stockholders. Reasons are many, perhaps one of them being that
people making decisions tend to own stock options or have bonuses tied
to stock performance of the companies they run.
This means that for a large, established tech company the product or
service it offers does not matter all that much anymore. It needs to be
just barely good enough to keep people using it. The easiest way to do
this is some form of a monopoly.
Monopoly is the business model of Silicon Valley, and
they are not even shy
about that
.
Monopoly as a business model
¶
If you ever tried moving an organization wholesale from Google
Workspace to Microsoft 365 (or
whatever it is called this
week
), you know what I mean.
These are two sets of office productivity services; on a basic level
their functionality is very similar. Mail, calendar, contacts, document
editing, access controls, and so on. And yet you can’t even directly
share a file from Google Workspace to a person who uses Microsoft 365
(or vice-versa) in a way that would allow them to access it within their
own service, using their existing account, without manually exporting
and importing the file.
Sidenote
¶
This lack of basic interoperability is not a technical necessity but
a business decision. For example,
Open Cloud
Mesh
protocol allows for a lot of interoperability between providers
of such office productivity services, and is implemented by
Nextcloud
.
What this means in practice is that two people with accounts on
different independently-run instances of any software implementing this
protocol, hosted at two different providers, could not only share, but
collaborate on a file – each from their own account, using a familiar
interface.
Someone confidently using one of the two largest online office suites
can quite reasonably feel completely lost when presented with the
interface of the other. Interoperability and data portability between
them seems like science fiction, to a point where it is genuinely
difficult for some people to even understand the concept.
Barriers to migration
¶
What this means in practice is that it does not matter if people
using their services
hate
them
– it only matters that they don’t hate them
strongly
enough
to want to go through hell of migrating over to some other
(or
the
other) provider.
With a barrier to migration between providers this high, people using
the service can be exploited in all sorts of ways they could not have
been otherwise.
Cory
Doctorow aptly calls that enshittification
.
At the same time, though, this also makes it really difficult for
service providers to compete on quality of the service or its features.
It’s not enough to have a product that is just
a bit
better
than the competition. It has to be
so much better
that it makes
it worthwhile for people to go through the hell of migrating over.
That’s a tough sell – that’s kind of the point of creating these
barriers in the first place.
And yet the line must go up. Somehow, tech companies need to convince
investors that their services are really becoming
so much
better
– so that they keep paying more and more for company
stock.
Enter the hype.
Learning to ride the Gartner
cycle
¶
Hype, of course, is nothing new.
Gartner even
made a graph about it
, a long time ago.
Using hype to sell products barely anyone actually needs for prices
that make no sense has a long and storied history – so much so that
“tulip mania” has basically become a cliché. Using hype to scam people
out of their money outright (instead of selling them something tangible,
albeit at an unreasonably inflated price) is also not particularly
innovative. Just ask
Elizabeth
Holmes
.
What’s new here, I think, is large, established companies using hype
not to push products or services, but to push their stock. And doing so
in unison, pumping the same bubble together.
Big Tech paid close attention to the cryptocurrency and NFT bubble.
They
tried
to
get
in
on it
, but they mostly failed. Probably the most useful thing that
emerged from the whole NFT frenzy was that Twitter’s
erstwhile
hexagonal profile pictures
for NFT holders
made it trivial to block
cryptobros
for a time.
Then, Facebook tried to manufacture their own hype bubble with
Metaverse, somewhat piggy-backing on NFTs – and even changing the
company name (
partially to
distract from their culpability in Rohingya genocide
). Metaverse was
inevitable
.
Anyone not on the Metaverse
would
unavoidably be left behind
.
Mark Zuckerberg bet the shop on that particular hype.
The
shop lost 46.5 billion-with-a-b USD
on it. Zuckerberg
took
“full responsibility” by firing eleven thousand people
.
Today
Meta
is pivoting to – you guessed it – AI
.

data.author: upofadown
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了即将发生的网络崩溃风险，将其比作"request smuggling"问题的重生。具体而言，通过发送带有两个Content-Length头的HTTP请求，可导致代理和服务器解析不一致，引发混乱。作者担心自己的HTTP/1.1服务器是否会受影响，但他的Go语言编写的代理和服务器因统一的请求解析方式，可能避免此问题。作者的代理在读取请求时，通过`ReadRequest`读取并做出重要决策，然后通过`Request.Write`发送至后端，且如Content-Length等特殊头信息不来自常规头映射，确保请求一致性。文章还批评了某些代理（如Akamai）生成无效请求的问题，强调若代理生成错误请求是严重错误。最终，作者等待验证其代理是否会因该问题而失效。

44737823.article_content:
polarizing parsers
The web as we know it will soon crash and burn in a fiery death. 12 days. There’s even a
countdown
. This is apparently a redux of
request smuggling reborn
. Request research reborn redux.
I was a little concerned, because I’ve got some HTTP/1.1 servers here, and oh no, what should I do? To very briefly summarize the original research (which is very interesting, especially some of the techniques for detecting and exploiting the flaw), they send an HTTP request with two Content-Length headers, and then one proxy reads a certain amount while a backend server reads a different amount. Chaos and madness ensue.
Can this happen here? My proxy is written in go, as are most of my servers. So the good news is they will probably parse all the requests the same way, but even so, I believe the design of my proxy makes this attack impossible. It reads a request with
ReadRequest
, takes a look at some headers like Host and Url to make important decisions, and then writes it to the appropriate backend with
Request.Write
. Reviewing the source code, special headers like Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding don’t even come from the normal header map.
Whatever the proxy request parser decides the request is, that’s what it becomes and that’s what the backend sees. Portswigger also found a poorly implemented access control bypass using two Host headers, which shouldn’t be possible. What I want to emphasize is that there’s no requirement that go follow any particular standard correctly. It can use the first header or the last header, but once the request has been parsed, it’s fixed. The logic that looks at the host to determine where this request is going next looks at exactly the same string that later gets put into the host header. That’s the only header that will appear on the wire. The parser has effectively polarized the input, and now everyone will see it the same way. The polarizer may be installed the wrong way around, but even so, the output is always coherent.
So what is Akamai (it’s always Akamai) doing that their proxy is putting invalid requests on the wire? Why are we blaming the protocol here, when it’s clear (to me) that the error is the proxy that sends invalid requests? If you put crap on the wire, that’s bad. If your supposed web firewall is the one putting crap on the wire, that’s really bad. Yes, someone somewhere has to deal with the crap input, but why is anything in your stack generating crap? That’s just deranged.
Anyway, 12 days to go, spooky countdown, and then I found out if my proxy is irredeemably broken and needs to die, or if this is just Akamai screwing up again.

Meka Agent
Meka Agent is an open-source, autonomous computer-using agent that delivers state-of-the-art browsing capabilities. The agent works and acts in the same way humans do, by purely using vision as its eyes and acting within a full computer context.
It is designed as a simple, extensible, and customizable framework, allowing flexibility in the choice of models, tools, and infrastructure providers.
Benchmarks
The agent primarily focuses on web browsing today, and achieves state-of-the-art benchmark results in the WebArena Benchmark (72.7%).
Read more
about the details of the benchmark results.
Meka App
If you would like to get started with browser automations without any setup, visit the
Meka App
to try the Meka Agent with $10 in free credits.
Getting Started
To get started with Meka, we packaged various providers that we have extensively tested. There are two main pieces:
A vision model that has
good visual grounding
. From our experimentation, OpenAI o3, Claude Sonnet 4, and Claude Opus 4 are the best US-based models. We have not experimented with Chinese-based models but would love to see contributions!
An infrastructure provider that exposes OS-level controls, not just a browser layer with Playwright screenshots. This is important for performance as a number of common web elements are rendered at the system level, invisible to the browser page. (Examples include dropdown menus, browser alerts, file uploads, and more)
To get started, we choose OpenAI o3 as the model and Anchor Browser as the VM-based infrastructure provider. We are open to submissions by other infra providers with OS-level controls!
Install the main components of the SDK
npm install @trymeka/core @trymeka/ai-provider-vercel @ai-sdk/openai @trymeka/computer-provider-anchor-browser playwright-core
Create your .env file and enter your API keys from the starter providers
OPENAI_API_KEY=GET FROM https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/api-keys
ANCHOR_BROWSER_API_KEY=GET FROM https://app.anchorbrowser.io/api-access
Start the agent

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM)，一种新型的递归神经网络架构，旨在解决AI中的复杂推理任务。HRM通过两个相互依赖的递归模块实现高效的层次化推理：负责慢速抽象规划的高层模块和处理快速详细计算的低层模块。HRM仅用2700万参数和1000个训练样本即可在复杂推理任务中表现出色，无需预训练或链式思考(CoT)数据。它在抽象与推理数据集(ARC)上超越了许多更大型的模型，展现了其在通用计算和推理系统中的潜力。文章还提供了安装指南、依赖项配置以及使用HRM进行实验的步骤，包括一个Sudoku解算器的快速演示。

Hierarchical Reasoning Model
Reasoning, the process of devising and executing complex goal-oriented action sequences, remains a critical challenge in AI.
Current large language models (LLMs) primarily employ Chain-of-Thought (CoT) techniques, which suffer from brittle task decomposition, extensive data requirements, and high latency. Inspired by the hierarchical and multi-timescale processing in the human brain, we propose the Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM), a novel recurrent architecture that attains significant computational depth while maintaining both training stability and efficiency.
HRM executes sequential reasoning tasks in a single forward pass without explicit supervision of the intermediate process, through two interdependent recurrent modules: a high-level module responsible for slow, abstract planning, and a low-level module handling rapid, detailed computations. With only 27 million parameters, HRM achieves exceptional performance on complex reasoning tasks using only 1000 training samples. The model operates without pre-training or CoT data, yet achieves nearly perfect performance on challenging tasks including complex Sudoku puzzles and optimal path finding in large mazes.
Furthermore, HRM outperforms much larger models with significantly longer context windows on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC), a key benchmark for measuring artificial general intelligence capabilities.
These results underscore HRM’s potential as a transformative advancement toward universal computation and general-purpose reasoning systems.
Quick Start Guide 🚀
Prerequisites ⚙️
Ensure PyTorch and CUDA are installed. The repo needs CUDA extensions to be built. If not present, run the following commands:
#
Install CUDA 12.6
CUDA_URL=https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.6.3/local_installers/cuda_12.6.3_560.35.05_linux.run
wget -q --show-progress --progress=bar:force:noscroll -O cuda_installer.run
$CUDA_URL
sudo sh cuda_installer.run --silent --toolkit --override
export
CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.6
#
Install PyTorch with CUDA 12.6
PYTORCH_INDEX_URL=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126
pip3 install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url
$PYTORCH_INDEX_URL
#
Additional packages for building extensions
pip3 install packaging ninja wheel setuptools setuptools-scm
Then install FlashAttention. For Hopper GPUs, install FlashAttention 3
git clone git@github.com:Dao-AILab/flash-attention.git
cd
flash-attention/hopper
python setup.py install
For Ampere or earlier GPUs, install FlashAttention 2
pip3 install flash-attn
Install Python Dependencies 🐍
pip install -r requirements.txt
W&B Integration 📈
This project uses
Weights & Biases
for experiment tracking and metric visualization. Ensure you're logged in:
wandb login
Run Experiments
Quick Demo: Sudoku Solver 💻🗲
Train a master-level Sudoku AI capable of solving extremely difficult puzzles on a modern laptop GPU. 🧩
#
Download and build Sudoku dataset
python dataset/build_sudoku_dataset.py --output-dir data/sudoku-extreme-1k-aug-1000  --subsample-size 1000 --num-aug 1000
#
Start training (single GPU, smaller batch size)
OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 python pretrain.py data_path=data/sudoku-extreme-1k-aug-1000 epochs=20000 eval_interval=2000 global_batch_size=384 lr=7e-5 puzzle_emb_lr=7e-5 weight_decay=1.0 puzzle_emb_weight_decay=1.0
Runtime: ~10 hours on a RTX 4070 laptop GPU
Trained Checkpoints 🚧
ARC-AGI-2
Sudoku 9x9 Extreme (1000 examples)
Maze 30x30 Hard (1000 examples)
To use the checkpoints, see Evaluation section below.
Full-scale Experiments 🔵
Experiments below assume an 8-GPU setup.
Dataset Preparation
#
Initialize submodules
git submodule update --init --recursive
#
ARC-1
python dataset/build_arc_dataset.py
#
ARC offical + ConceptARC, 960 examples
#
ARC-2
python dataset/build_arc_dataset.py --dataset-dirs dataset/raw-data/ARC-AGI-2/data --output-dir data/arc-2-aug-1000
#
ARC-2 official, 1120 examples
#
Sudoku-Extreme
python dataset/build_sudoku_dataset.py
#
Full version
python dataset/build_sudoku_dataset.py --output-dir data/sudoku-extreme-1k-aug-1000  --subsample-size 1000 --num-aug 10

data.title: Scammers unleash flood of online gaming sites
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
诈骗者利用Discord和其他社交媒体平台发布大量精美的在线游戏和赌博网站广告，通过提供免费积分吸引用户，最终盗取用户存入的加密货币。这些骗局通常冒用知名网红如Mr. Beast的名义，宣称与其有合作，并提供2500美元的积分奖励。用户需创建账户才能领取积分，玩精美的视频游戏，但当试图提现“奖金”时，网站要求进行“验证存款”，即存入约100美元的加密货币。然而，显示的“奖金”是虚假的，存款后资金再也无法取回。

这些骗局涉及超过1200个诈骗网站，使用相同的技术基础设施和API密钥，且通过独特的比特币钱包接收资金，阻止用户提现。受害者还可能受到自称“追款专家”的二次诈骗。骗子通过追踪IP地址和设备信息，防止用户在多个网站重复注册，显示这些网站由同一实体操控。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对在线诈骗，特别是与加密货币和在线赌博相关的骗局，用户的讨论和反应。

不同观点：
• [tantalor] 和 [chihuahua] 认为这种要求提前支付加密货币的行为是一种典型的“提前收费诈骗”（advance fee scam），是历史悠久的骗局。他们对此表现出明显的警惕和反感，认为这种骗局非常明显。

• [nottorp] 纠正了话题的方向，指出这是在线赌博（gambling）而不是一般的在线游戏（gaming），强调了讨论的具体背景。

• [JoeOfTexas] 分享了自己尝试建立合法游戏门户的经历，指出这些诈骗网站往往技术上和设计上都做得很好，暗示背后可能有专业团队操作。

• [MattSayar] 提到了与“杀猪盘”诈骗相关的短信减少的现象，并好奇这种变化是因为情况有所改善还是仅仅是因为自己运气好。

• [mathgradthrow] 讽刺地评论加密货币交易容易逆转，暗示实际上并非如此，强调了加密货币交易的不可逆性，进一步指出了受害者可能面临的追讨困难。

• [dylan604] 引用了他人的话，指出这种诈骗行为是一个有组织的犯罪活动，具有可扩展的操作模式和技术痕迹，暗示背后有复杂的诈骗网络，而不仅仅是单个网站的行为。

• [MOARDONGZPLZ] 质疑参与可疑在线赌博的人群，并暗示受害者在某种程度上也应为自己的损失承担责任，表现出对受害者的批评态度。

补充讨论：
• 诈骗技术的复杂性和专业性：[JoeOfTexas] 提到这些诈骗网站在技术和设计上都非常成熟，暗示背后有专业团队操作，使得这些骗局更难被识别和打击。

• 诈骗活动的组织性和规模：[dylan604] 指出这些诈骗行为并非孤立事件，而是一个有组织的犯罪活动，具有明确的操作模式和基础设施，进一步强调了打击这种行为的复杂性。

• 受害者责任的争议：[MOARDONGZPLZ] 的评论引发了关于受害者在诈骗事件中责任的讨论，这种观点可能会引起争议，因为其他人可能认为受害者不应被责备。

争议的焦点：
• 受害者是否应为自己的损失承担部分责任：[MOARDONGZPLZ] 的观点与对受害者的同情态度形成对比，可能引发关于如何平衡受害者责任和外部打击诈骗的讨论。

44738132.article_content:
Fraudsters are flooding Discord and other social media platforms with ads for hundreds of polished online gaming and wagering websites that lure people with free credits and eventually abscond with any cryptocurrency funds deposited by players. Here’s a closer look at the social engineering tactics and remarkable traits of this sprawling network of more than 1,200 scam sites.
The scam begins with deceptive ads posted on social media that claim the wagering sites are working in partnership with popular social media personalities, such as
Mr. Beast
, who recently launched a gaming business called
Beast Games
. The ads invariably state that by using a supplied “promo code,” interested players can claim a $2,500 credit on the advertised gaming website.
An ad posted to a Discord channel for a scam gambling website that the proprietors falsely claim was operating in collaboration with the Internet personality Mr. Beast. Image: Reddit.com.
The gaming sites all require users to create a free account to claim their $2,500 credit, which they can use to play any number of extremely polished video games that ask users to bet on each action. At the scam website gamblerbeast[.]com, for example, visitors can pick from dozens of games like
B-Ball Blitz
, in which you play a basketball pro who is taking shots from the free throw line against a single opponent, and you bet on your ability to sink each shot.
The financial part of this scam begins when users try to cash out any “winnings.” At that point, the gaming site will reject the request and prompt the user to make a “verification deposit” of cryptocurrency — typically around $100 — before any money can be distributed. Those who deposit cryptocurrency funds are soon asked for additional payments.
However, any “winnings” displayed by these gaming sites are a complete fantasy, and players who deposit cryptocurrency funds will never see that money again. Compounding the problem, victims likely will soon be peppered with come-ons from “recovery experts” who peddle dubious claims on social media networks about being able to retrieve funds lost to such scams.
KrebsOnSecurity first learned about this network of phony betting sites from a Discord user who asked to be identified only by their screen name: “
Thereallo
” is a 17-year-old developer who operates multiple Discord servers and said they began digging deeper after users started complaining of being inundated with misleading spam messages promoting the sites.
“We were being spammed relentlessly by these scam posts from compromised or purchased [Discord] accounts,” Thereallo said. “I got frustrated with just banning and deleting, so I started to investigate the infrastructure behind the scam messages. This is not a one-off site, it’s a scalable criminal enterprise with a clear playbook, technical fingerprints, and financial infrastructure.”
After comparing the code on the gaming sites promoted via spam messages, Thereallo found they all invoked the same API key for an online chatbot that appears to be in limited use or else is custom-made. Indeed, a scan for that API key at the threat hunting platform
Silent Push
reveals at least 1,270 recently-registered and active domains whose names all invoke some type of gaming or wagering theme.
The “verification deposit” stage of the scam requires the user to deposit cryptocurrency in order to withdraw their “winnings.”
Thereallo said the operators of this scam empire appear to generate a unique Bitcoin wallet for each gaming domain they deploy.
“This is a decoy wallet,” Thereallo explained. “Once the victim deposits funds, they are never able to withdraw any money. Any attempts to contact the ‘Live Support’ are handled by a combination of AI and human operators who eventually block the user. The chat system is self-hosted, making it difficult to report to third-party service providers.”
Thereallo discovered another feature common to all of these scam gambling sites [hereafter referred to simply as “scambling” sites]: If you register at one of them and then very quickly try to register at a sister property of theirs from the same Internet address and device, the registration request is denied at the second site.
“I registered on one site, then hopped to another to register again,” Thereallo said. Instead, the second site returned an error stating that a new account couldn’t be created for another 10 minutes.
The scam gaming site spinora dot cc shares the same chatbot API as more than 1,200 similar fake gaming sites.
“They’re tracking my VPN IP across their entire network,” Thereallo explained. “My password manager also proved it. It tried to use my dummy email on a site I had never visited, and the site told me the account already existed. So it’s definitely one entity running a single platform with 1,200+ different domain names as front-ends. This explains how their support works, a central pool of agents handling all the sites. It also explains why they’re so strict about not givi

data.title: The game is almost over for one of Hong Kong's last mahjong carvers
data.author: rectang
data.article_summary: Ho Sau-Mei是香港仅存的几位麻将雕刻师之一，从事这一行已有四十多年。她从13岁开始跟父亲学习手艺，如今视力和体力大不如前，但仍坚持在红磡的小店里手工雕刻麻将牌。她的店铺狭窄简陋，工作台是一块玻璃展示柜。尽管麻将制作已大多被中国内地工厂取代，她仍使用传统工具，以精湛技艺雕刻、上色，完成一套手工麻将需10到14天，售价245美元。香港政府在2014年将麻将雕刻列入“非物质文化遗产”，但如今香港仅剩寥寥几位匠人，而她是唯一一位仍在工作的女性。尽管年近古稀，她继续工作以避免无聊，但承认体力大不如前。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对故事中人物的评价和态度

不同观点：
• [littlekey] 的观点：虽然认为故事本身不错，但指出故事中的主人公应该更好地管理订单。他建议可能需要有人帮忙，暗示主人公在某些方面可能存在不足，特别是在工作效率或管理上。

• [Hackbraten] 的观点：对故事中的商店和主人公持完全 positive 的态度，称赞其为“了不起的商店和女人”，没有提出任何批评或改进建议，而是表达了赞赏和支持。

补充讨论：
• 两种观点之间存在一定的态度对比。[littlekey] 更关注实际操作中的管理问题，提出了建设性建议，而 [Hackbraten] 则更倾向于总体上的认可和赞扬。
• 争议的焦点可能在于对主人公能力的评价上。[littlekey] 认为她需要帮助，而 [Hackbraten] 则认为她已经非常出色，无需进一步改进。
• 总体来看，评论中的讨论反映了人们对同一故事的不同关注点，一些人关注细节和管理，另一些人则更注重整体印象和情感。

44702325.article_content:
The game is almost over for one of Hong Kongâs last mahjong carvers
Story by Kathleen Magramo, CNN
Photographs and video by Noemi Cassanelli, CNN
Published July 27, 2025
Ho Sau-Mei, one of Hong Kongâs last mahjong tile carvers, is getting old. âMy eyesight is fading, and my hands are getting sore,â she says brusquely as she chisels the intricate strokes of a Chinese character or the petals of a flower onto a piece of plastic little bigger than a postage stamp.
For over four decades, Ho has been carving mahjong tiles in a tiny roadside shop in Hung Hom, an old harborside district that is now seeing the rapid construction of shiny, new residential high-rises.
She started learning the craft at age 13 from her father, who founded the family's tile business, Kam Fat Mahjong, in 1962. Masters who would visit Hong Kong during its manufacturing heyday in the 1970s and 80s also shared their techniques and trained apprentices.
Ho Sau-Mei carves mahjong tiles at her shop in Hong Kong.
Mahjong is a game for four people similar to rummy and is hugely popular across China and among Chinese communities for which it also serves as a cultural ritual and symbol of tradition. Children learn how to play as they spend time with cousins and friends over Lunar New Year, and among the elderly itâs popular all year round.
Mahjong tiles are traditionally made of wood, ivory or bamboo, with tile makers cutting, polishing, carving and coloring each piece.
In the 1960s, there were more than 20 mahjong tile carvers in Hong Kong â and even an association dedicated to the industry.
Now most mahjong tiles are mass-produced in factories in mainland China.
Mahjong tiles are stacked on a game table in Hong Kong.
The craft was listed as an âintangible cultural heritageâ by the Hong Kong government in 2014, which provides funding for research into and preservation of various protected traditions.
But less than a handful of mahjong artisans are still around the city, and among them Ho is the only woman left practicing the craft.
A craft of precision
Minibuses and double-decker buses zoom past the busy road across her dimly lit ground-floor shop beneath a staircase on Bulkeley Street.
The store is barely two meters wide with a grimy glass case on the wall that reaches the ceiling filled with faded photographs and stacks of novelty mahjong tiles. Hovering behind Hoâs work stool is a shrine that glows a gentle red hue.
Ho starts to carve mahjong tiles in the morning.
Pictures of Ho can be found inside her shop.
Workers from nearby hardware stores and elderly people sheâs befriended over the years also banter with her. Pedestrians sometimes slow down to observe Ho deep in work hunched over her small working space.
Hoâs routine has stayed the same even as the neighborhood developed, with mahjong tiles now mostly made by big factories in mainland China.
Sheâs usually already seated at the storefront and lays out her tools for the day just before 10 a.m.
At 68 years old, Ho says she only works until about noon these days, sighing that she âdoesnât have the staminaâ to carve away all day anymore. She could retire if she wanted to, she says, âbut Iâll get bored.â
She lays out the Bakelite tiles lined neatly on a heavy wooden tray and prepares her specialized tools on the tiny glass display case that serves as her work desk.
Tiles are packaged inside Hoâs shop in Hong Kong.
Ho uses a traditional tool to carve a tile.
A complete mahjong set comes with 144 tiles, including the four suits â bamboo, dots, characters, directional winds (north, south, east and west) â and special tiles depicting flowers, dragons and the four seasons.
One of Hoâs tools resembles a giant corkscrew and is used to drill the concentric circles on one of the rectangles.
Using other tools with varying tips and angles, she holds the blank tiles with her calloused thumb and middle finger and masterfully etches the complicated Chinese characters and flower tiles with surgical precision.
Ho paints mahjong tiles inside her store.
For the penultimate process, Ho brings out vintage jars of paint, their labels weathered by time. âDonât go away, this part is fast,â Ho tells us.
She brushes red, green and blue colors onto the naked tiles, carefully bringing the engraved symbols to life.
A full set costs $245 and takes around 10 to 14 days to make by hand. But if youâre planning to order a set from Ho, the entire process is still analogue â and somewhat haphazard.
The phone rings a few times during the day with a handful of customers inquiring about the orders theyâve placed.  But Ho doesnât really keep track of the orders.
A client speaks with Ho and her assistant.
Mahjong tiles are seen in front of a small house temple at Hoâs shop.
Thereâs no online booking system. Everything is done either by phone or in person, and she scribbles the orders down on a notebook thatâs torn apart at the spine.

data.title: A Dive into Open Chat Protocols
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了网站管理员使用Anubis系统来保护服务器免受AI公司大规模抓取数据导致的过载影响。Anubis采用了一种类似于Hashcash的“工作量证明”机制，在个人用户访问时几乎不增加负担，但在面对大规模抓取时则会显著增加成本。这一方案是一个临时解决办法，旨在为更复杂的身份验证技术争取时间。同时，文章提醒用户Anubis需要现代JavaScript功能，因此需禁用如JShelter等可能阻止这些功能的插件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放聊天协议及其使用中的问题

不同观点：
• PaulHoule认为，为了展示对AI爬虫的反对而故意让观众等待，是一种做作且让用户体验变差的行为。他明确反对通过让用户不便来表达立场，尤其提到了大科技公司通常采用这种让人不满的方式。
• 尽管PaulHoule批评了故意让用户不便的做法，但他同时指出，开放聊天协议是去"去垃圾化"（de-enshittification）难题中非常有趣且关键的一部分。他认可开放协议的技术潜力，并认为它们在技术社区中具有实际价值。

补充讨论：
• PaulHoule提到了XMPP协议，尽管它被认为"不够酷"，但在特定领域（如军队和警察）中非常流行。他给出的例子包括将XMPP定制用于存储与公众互动的信息，或者用于战地报告。这表明某些技术在特定专业环境中具有实用性，尽管在大众文化中并不受欢迎。
• 争议的焦点在于如何在不损害用户体验的前提下表达对某些技术（如AI爬虫）的反对，以及开放协议在广泛应用中的实际表现和认知差距。

44738216.article_content:
Making sure you're not a bot!
Loading...
Why am I seeing this?
You are seeing this because the administrator of this website has set up
Anubis
to protect the server against the scourge of
AI companies aggressively scraping websites
. This can and does cause downtime for the websites, which makes their resources inaccessible for everyone.
Anubis is a compromise. Anubis uses a
Proof-of-Work
scheme in the vein of
Hashcash
, a proposed proof-of-work scheme for reducing email spam. The idea is that at individual scales the additional load is ignorable, but at mass scraper levels it adds up and makes scraping much more expensive.
Ultimately, this is a hack whose real purpose is to give a "good enough" placeholder solution so that more time can be spent on fingerprinting and identifying headless browsers (EG: via how they do font rendering) so that the challenge proof of work page doesn't need to be presented to users that are much more likely to be legitimate.
Please note that Anubis requires the use of modern JavaScript features that plugins like
JShelter
will disable. Please disable JShelter or other such plugins for this domain.

data.title: Launch HN: Hyprnote (YC S25) – An open-source AI meeting notetaker
data.author: yujonglee
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕新推出软件"Hyprnote"的功能、技术实现、商业模式、隐私及企业应用的讨论。

不同观点：
• 一些用户对项目宣传中列出的大公司客户表示怀疑，认为这些公司不太可能通过艰苦的销售获得（itsalotoffun）。
• 一位用户对AI会议记录软件需要高端LLM模型和订阅表示不解，并提到自己使用本地化工具组合来完成类似任务，对Hyprnote的本地化和开源表示赞赏，但关注API和扩展性（yonl）。
• 另一位用户在Linux上构建时遇到需要多个API密钥的问题，对本地优先的软件需要这么多API密钥感到意外（polyaniline）。
• 关于商业模式，有用户希望了解软件的盈利计划，特别是提到YC投资背景，担心未来收费功能（teiferer）。另一位用户同样关注商业模式，尤其在开源情况下如何吸引非技术用户（mentalgear）。
• 一些用户对软件的实际使用效果表示满意，认为其满足了自己的需求，并表示会继续使用（Myrmornis）。
• 有用户指出软件在多人会议中的发言者识别功能不足，认为这是继续使用的一个障碍（ljosa）。
• 另一位用户关注实时转录的准确性与延迟之间的平衡，提到其他工具在这方面的优势（btown）。
• 有用户希望软件能达到MacWhisper的功能水平，特别是自动会议检测和定制转录操作，并提出项目标签等新功能建议（crashabr）。
• 一位正在构建语音控制应用的用户关心回声消除功能的技术选择，特别是平台特定的API使用情况（AlexErrant）。
• 关于隐私问题，一位用户担心软件发送到Sentry的数据量（shepardrtc）。
• 一位Mac用户在下载安装后遇到启动问题，给予权限后仍无法打开软件（p2hari）。
• 有企业用户关注智能同意管理功能，特别是在法律要求披露录音的情况下如何减少对用户体验的影响（theodorewiles）。
• 另一位用户询问是否计划与Apple Notes应用集成（believ3）。
• 一位用户对Granola工具的隐私设置表示不满，特别是笔记自动公开的问题（eawgewag）。

补充讨论：
• 用户对本地优先、开源和隐私的重视反映了对软件控制权和数据安全的关注。
• 关于实时转录和发言者识别的技术挑战是用户体验中的关键问题。
• 商业模式的透明度是用户在考虑采用软件时的重要考量因素，特别是在开源和免费功能之外如何实现盈利。
• 不同用户的技术背景和使用场景导致了对软件功能和易用性的多样化需求。

data.title: Meta shares jump on strong results as Zuckerberg sets out SI goals
data.author: guiambros
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta（Facebook母公司）的广告收入是否合理，以及广告效果是否被验证。

不同观点：
• [ed_mercer]认为Meta的巨额广告收入难以理解，因为他周围几乎没有年轻人使用Facebook，质疑广告的有效性和收入的真实性。
• [belter]支持[ed_mercer]的观点，表示自己及周围的新生代都不使用Facebook，并提出疑问：是否公司只在广告上花钱而未验证广告效果，同时呼吁对Meta的收入数据进行更深入的分析以揭示客户群体。

补充讨论：
• 质疑Meta广告收入的真实性，核心论据是个人观察到的新生代不使用Facebook的现象，与Meta声称的广告收入规模形成对比。
• 讨论焦点在于广告效果的验证缺失和收入数据的透明性，尤其是对Meta广告客户群体的具体构成存在疑问。
• 提出需要“forensic analysis”（取证分析）来进一步理解Meta广告收入的合理性，表明对当前数据和解释的不信任。

Tesla
Tesla Model S
Tesla stops taking Model S/X orders in Europe
Fred Lambert
| Jul 30 2025 - 8:10 am PT
64 Comments
Tesla has stopped taking new orders for its flagship Model S and Model X vehicles in Europe. It’s not the first time it happened, but it still raises questions.
Following the 2021 Model S/X refresh, Tesla ceased taking new orders for the vehicles in Europe for an unexpectedly long period.
The refreshed models were unveiled in January 2021, and Tesla continued to take orders through December 2021, after which they stopped.
It didn’t
reopen orders in Europe until August 2022
.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Now, something similar is happening with the new refresh.
In June,
Tesla unveiled another minor refresh of the Model S and Model X
.
Now, just over a month later, Tesla has stopped taking new orders for the Model S and Model X in Europe. The automaker deactivated the online configurators and instead, it redirects to the main Model S and Model X pages, where buyers can still find some inventory vehicles.
At this time, the reason for the stoppage in taking orders is unclear, but it may be due to a supply issue.
Tesla only produces Model S and Model X vehicles at its Fremont factory in California. With the last refresh, Tesla had difficulties ramping up production.
Now, Tesla has significantly reduced its production capacity for these vehicle programs, as
demand has declined over the last few years
.
Currently, Tesla quotes a 2-month wait time to receive a new, made-to-order Model S in California.
Electrek’s Take
Top comment by
Philip234
Liked by 13 people
According to Electrive, "The German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) recorded just 58 new Model S and 59 new Model X registrations in the first half of the year..." If the EU's biggest market is only buying 10 of each model a month, it is probably no longer worthwhile to go through the homologation expense.
View all comments
When the lead time for ordering is too long, as it currently could be in Europe, and California is at 2 months, Tesla has sometimes shut down new orders.
It could be as simple as that.
Tesla needs to ramp up Model S/X production after the refresh to meet demand in North America before returning to Europe.
The automaker could also be careful about locking in a price for Model S/X months in advance. The US is now imposing 15% tariffs on Japan, where Model S/X battery cells are produced. The situation has been fluid, making it hard for Tesla to predict costs.

By
Matthew Hutson
21 hours ago
Some sci-fi scenarios depict robots as cold-hearted clankers eager to
manipulate
human stooges. But that’s not the only possible path for artificial intelligence.
Humans have evolved emotions like anger, sadness and gratitude to help us think, interact and build mutual trust. Advanced AI could do the same. In populations of simple software agents (like characters in “The Sims” but much, much simpler),
having “guilt” can be a stable strategy
that benefits them and increases cooperation, researchers report July 30 in
Journal of the Royal Society Interface.
Sign up for our newsletter
We summarize the week's scientific breakthroughs every Thursday.
Emotions are not just subjective feelings but bundles of cognitive biases, physiological responses and behavioral tendencies. When we harm someone, we often feel compelled to pay a penance, perhaps as a signal to others that we won’t offend again. This drive for self-punishment can be called guilt, and it’s how the researchers programmed it into their agents. The question was whether those that had it would be outcompeted by those that didn’t, say Theodor Cimpeanu, a computer scientist at the University of Stirling in Scotland, and colleagues.
The agents played a two-player game with their neighbors called iterated prisoner’s dilemma. The game has roots in
game theory
, a mathematical framework for analyzing multiple decision makers’ choices based on their preferences and individual strategies. On each turn, each player “cooperates” (plays nice) or “defects” (acts selfishly). In the short term, you win the most points by defecting, but that tends to make your partner start defecting, so everyone is better off cooperating in the long run. The AI agents couldn’t feel guilt as richly as humans do but experienced it as a self-imposed penalty that nudges them to cooperate after selfish behavior.
The researchers ran several simulations with different settings and social network structures. In each, the 900 players were each assigned one of six strategies defining their tendency to defect and to feel and respond to guilt. In one strategy, nicknamed DGCS for technical reasons, the agent felt guilt after defecting, meaning that it gave up points until it cooperated again. Critically, the AI agent felt guilt (lost points) only if it received information that its partner was also paying a guilt price after defecting. This prevented the agent from being a patsy, thus enforcing cooperation in others. (In the real world, seeing guilt in others can be tricky, but costly apologies are a good sign.)
The simulations didn’t model how guiltlike behavior might first emerge — only whether it could survive and spread once introduced. After each turn, agents could copy a neighbor’s strategy, with a probability of imitation based on neighbors’ cumulative score. In many scenarios — particularly when guilt was relatively low-cost and agents interacted with only their neighbors — DGCS became the dominant strategy, and most interactions became cooperative, the researchers found.
We may want to program the capacity for guilt or other emotions into AIs. “Maybe it’s easier to trust when you have a feeling that the agent also thinks in the same way that you think,” Cimpeanu says. We may also witness emotions — at least the functional aspects, even if not the conscious ones — emerge on their own in groups of AIs if they can
mutate or self-program
, he says. As AIs proliferate, they could comprehend the cold logic to human warmth.
But there are caveats, says Sarita Rosenstock, a philosopher at The University of Melbourne in Australia who was not involved in the work but has used game theory to
study guilt’s evolution
. First, simulations embody many assumptions, so one can’t draw strong conclusions from a single study. But this paper contributes “an exploration of the possibility space,” highlighting areas where guilt is and is not sustainable, she says.
Second, it’s hard to map simulations like these to the real world. What counts as a verifiable cost for an AI, besides paying actual money from a coffer? If you talk to a present-day chatbot, she says, “it’s basically free for it to say I’m sorry.” With no
transparency
into its innards, a
misaligned
AI might feign remorse, only to trespass again.

data.article_summary: MacFriends 是一个能让现代Mac电脑控制旧款Macintosh Classic的工具。通过一个Arduino设备，用户可以使用MacBook的触控板或鼠标移动Macintosh Classic上的光标，并进行键盘输入。其工作原理是当鼠标触及屏幕左侧时，光标会被锁定，移动和按键信息通过Arduino经由USB串口发送到Macintosh Classic。Arduino代码使用platform.io编译，macOS应用则通过Xcode构建。连接方面，ADB数据线接Arduino数字引脚2，电源线接5V，地线接GND。项目创建者表示该项目更多是概念验证，并不完美，且由于已购新鼠标，不会继续更新。

MacFriends: Universal Control for your old Macintosh Classic
A Universal Control-esque app and Arduino thingy for controlling your old Macintosh Classic from a modern Mac.
Features
Mouse Control
: Move the mouse cursor on your Macintosh Classic using your MacBook's trackpad or mouse.
Keyboard Input
: You can type and even do ⌘+Z!
Setting view
for configuring the serial port. What more do you want to configure?
How it works
When the mouse touches the left edge of the screen, the cursor will be locked and the movement and keystrokes will be sent via an Arduino.
The Arduino (uno or nano. I'm using a nano) is listens via USB serial for mouse and keyboard events from the Mac and sends them to the Macintosh Classic over ADB.
Using
The Arduino code can be compiled using platform.io. The macos app can be built using Xcode.
On the Arduino side, connect the ADB data line to Arduino's digital pin 2. Connect the ADB power line to Arduino's 5V pin and the ADB ground line to Arduino's GND pin.
Why don't just buy a new old mouse?
I just did, so I'm not updating this project anymore. But if your mouse is broken, you can use this project to control your old Macintosh Classic from a MacBook.
Disclaimer
The code is not perfect, it's more a proof of concept than a production-ready solution.
At least it's not vibe coded.
The Arduino ADB code is based on
ADBuino
. The macOS app is written in Swift and uses the
SwiftSerial
library for serial communication and
BitByteData
for serializing data to the Arduino.

data.title: '70 MPH e-bikes' prompt one US state to change its laws
data.author: harambae
data.article_summary: 美国康涅狄格州因青少年骑高速电动自行车（e-bikes）现象日益增多，正修订法律加以规范。一些电动自行车出厂时速度限制在30英里/小时（约48公里/小时），但经过改装后可达到60至70英里/小时（约96至112公里/小时）。警方表示，这类改装非常容易，网上有许多教程。为此，州政府决定更新法律，规定功率超过750W的电动自行车将被视为“机动车辆”，需要驾驶执照；功率超过3500W的则被视为摩托车，需摩托车执照、注册和保险。新法预计于10月生效。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电动自行车（e-bike）的速度限制、法规管理以及安全问题

不同观点：
• **支持速度限制和法规管理**：
   - [habosa] 支持将电动自行车的辅助速度限制在20mph以下，认为这样可以减少因高速行驶导致的危险行为。他提到一些人使用高功率电动自行车在城市中超速行驶（30mph+），违反交通规则，如逆行、骑在人行道上、发短信等，存在安全隐患。
   - [throw0101c] 支持欧洲的电动自行车法规（ pedal assist 速度限制在15.5mph，电机功率不超过250W），认为超过这个限制的车辆应被视为轻便摩托车，并需相应驾照。
   - [foxyv] 和 [droopyEyelids] 也支持对电动自行车进行注册和牌照管理，类似于轻便摩托车的管理方式，以确保安全和合法使用。

• **对法规执行和实际效果的质疑**：
   - [potato3732842] 认为超速问题是一个“自我解决的问题”，不需要额外法律。他认为在城市中以过高速度骑行本身就非常危险，人们自然会避免。同时提到，执法不严导致即使有法律也难以实施。
   - [mPReDiToR] 指出，由于警力不足，很多地方对电动自行车的法规执行不力，导致人们普遍无视法规。除非出现严重事故，否则很少有人会去追究。

• **关于车辆分类的争议**：
   - [daft_pink] 指出一些电动自行车（如Super 73）宣称符合Class 1和Class 2的规则，但实际上可以通过设置切换到不受限的速度模式，这违反了自行车法规，应被视为摩托车。
   - [zaphar] 直接指出，任何速度超过常规自行车限度的车辆应被归类为电动摩托车，而不是电动自行车。

• **个人经验与技术修改的讨论**：
   - [extr] 分享了自己对电动自行车进行技术修改以提高速度的经验，并指出在城市中很少有执法，但在郊区则会有更多关注和执法。他还提到年龄和驾驶执照可能影响执法人员的处理方式。
   - [BizarroLand] 购买了高功率电动自行车，认为有必要对高功率车型进行管理，以避免危险。他同时希望这些车辆不会被完全禁止，因为它们在某些情况下非常有用和有趣。

• **市场和法律漏洞的讨论**：
   - [shkkmo] 认为市场上有大量电动自行车可以通过简单修改（特别是软件修改）轻易超过法律规定的速度限制，这表明现行法规存在漏洞，需要更严格的监管。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于如何平衡电动自行车的便利性与安全性，特别是在城市交通环境中。一些人认为需要更严格的法规和管理，而另一些人则认为市场和个人行为最终会自我调节，法规执行不力是主要问题。

44736501.article_content:
ebikes
’70 MPH e-bikes’ prompt one US state to change its laws
Micah Toll
| Jul 29 2025 - 3:52 am PT
66 Comments
Electric bikes are booming in popularity in just about every demographic in the US. From teens riding to school all the way to elderly folks getting back on a bicycle for the first time in years, electric bikes are becoming ubiquitous. But as speeds and power levels have increased, Connecticut is responding with new laws.
Westport Police Lt. Serenity Dobson recently spoke to
CTInsider
about the phenomenon of more teens riding their e-bikes to school instead of being driven by their parents. “The whole entire bike rack is filled with these bikes that look like electric dirt bikes.”
Moped-style e-bikes have become increasingly popular with teens, with companies like Super73 ushering in a new wave of electric bikes with design cues borrowed from classic mopeds of decades past.
But Dobson says that these e-bikes are too easily modifiable, increasing speed and motor power past acceptable limits.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
“These bikes come stock at 30 mph, but you can cut the controller, and so then they can go 60, 70 mph, and the kids know how to do this,” Dobson said, adding that there has been a “huge increase in middle school-aged kids” riding e-bikes, particularly in the summer when school is out. “There are a lot of YouTube videos where it can show you how easy it is for someone to modify it.”
Top comment by
John W Campbell
Liked by 7 people
750W seems to be a good cut off between E-bikes, and basically motorcycles. Anything that can go over 30 mph should be classified as a motorcycle.
View all comments
It’s not clear that such speeds are actually capable on stock parts from nearly any electric bicycle, and legal electric bikes are not capable of exceeding either 20 or 28 mph, depending on their classification, but Dobson may be referring to Sur Ron-style electric motorbikes, which are off-road electric motorcycles that look like small dirt bikes.
Connecticut already uses the common three-class system that codifies legal e-bikes as up to 20 mph (32 km/h) and 750W (one horsepower) for Class 1 and 2, or up to 28 mph (45 km/h) for Class 3 e-bikes.
But now the state is updating its e-bike laws, adding that any e-bike with over 750W of power will be considered a “motor-driven cycle” and require a driver’s license. Over 3,500W? That will be considered a motorcycle and require a motorcycle endorsement to legally ride, as well as registration and insurance like a motorcycle.
The new laws are expected to come into effect in October.

data.title: Linux Performance Analysis (2015)
data.author: benjacksondev
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了在Linux服务器上进行性能分析时，如何利用前60秒快速获取系统资源使用情况。通过运行十个标准Linux命令，可以初步了解系统性能问题。这些命令包括：

1. **uptime**：查看系统负载，了解CPU和I/O需求。
2. **dmesg | tail**：查看最近的系统消息，寻找错误。
3. **vmstat 1**：监控CPU、内存、I/O等资源的使用和饱和度。
4. **mpstat -P ALL 1**：查看每个CPU的使用情况。
5. **pidstat 1**：查看各个进程的资源使用情况。
6. **iostat -xz 1**：分析设备I/O性能。
7. **free -m**：查看内存使用情况。
8. **sar -n DEV 1**：监控网络接口。
9. **sar -n TCP,ETCP 1**：分析TCP和网络性能。
10. **top**：动态查看系统整体资源使用情况。

这些命令帮助快速识别系统资源（CPU、内存、磁盘等）的利用率、饱和度和错误，从而定位性能瓶颈。在Netflix的EC2 Linux环境中，这些工具对分析和解决问题至关重要。

Linux Performance Analysis in 60,000 Milliseconds
Netflix Technology Blog
11 min read
·
Nov 30, 2015
--
11
Listen
Share
You log in to a Linux server with a performance issue: what do you check in the first minute?
At Netflix we have a massive EC2 Linux cloud, and numerous performance analysis tools to monitor and investigate its performance. These include
Atlas
for cloud-wide monitoring, and
Vector
for on-demand instance analysis. While those tools help us solve most issues, we sometimes need to login to an instance and run some standard Linux performance tools.
First 60 Seconds: Summary
In this post, the Netflix Performance Engineering team will show you the first 60 seconds of an optimized performance investigation at the command line, using standard Linux tools you should have available. In 60 seconds you can get a high level idea of system resource usage and running processes by running the following ten commands. Look for errors and saturation metrics, as they are both easy to interpret, and then resource utilization. Saturation is where a resource has more load than it can handle, and can be exposed either as the length of a request queue, or time spent waiting.
uptime
dmesg | tail
vmstat 1
mpstat -P ALL 1
pidstat 1
iostat -xz 1
free -m
sar -n DEV 1
sar -n TCP,ETCP 1
top
Some of these commands require the sysstat package installed. The metrics these commands expose will help you complete some of the
USE Method
: a methodology for locating performance bottlenecks. This involves checking utilization, saturation, and error metrics for all resources (CPUs, memory, disks, e.t.c.). Also pay attention to when you have checked and exonerated a resource, as by process of elimination this narrows the targets to study, and directs any follow on investigation.
The following sections summarize these commands, with examples from a production system. For more information about these tools, see their man pages.
1. uptime
$
uptime
23:51:26 up 21:31, 1 user, load average: 30.02, 26.43, 19.02
This is a quick way to view the load averages, which indicate the number of tasks (processes) wanting to run. On Linux systems, these numbers include processes wanting to run on CPU, as well as processes blocked in uninterruptible I/O (usually disk I/O). This gives a high level idea of resource load (or demand), but can’t be properly understood without other tools. Worth a quick look only.
The three numbers are exponentially damped moving sum averages with a 1 minute, 5 minute, and 15 minute constant. The three numbers give us some idea of how load is changing over time. For example, if you’ve been asked to check a problem server, and the 1 minute value is much lower than the 15 minute value, then you might have logged in too late and missed the issue.
In the example above, the load averages show a recent increase, hitting 30 for the 1 minute value, compared to 19 for the 15 minute value. That the numbers are this large means a lot of something: probably CPU demand; vmstat or mpstat will confirm, which are commands 3 and 4 in this sequence.
2. dmesg | tail
$
dmesg | tail
[1880957.563150] perl invoked oom-killer: gfp_mask=0x280da, order=0, oom_score_adj=0
[...]
[1880957.563400] Out of memory: Kill process 18694 (perl) score 246 or sacrifice child
[1880957.563408] Killed process 18694 (perl) total-vm:1972392kB, anon-rss:1953348kB, file-rss:0kB
[2320864.954447] TCP: Possible SYN flooding on port 7001. Dropping request.  Check SNMP counters.
This views the last 10 system messages, if there are any. Look for errors that can cause performance issues. The example above includes the oom-killer, and TCP dropping a request.
Don’t miss this step! dmesg is always worth checking.
3. vmstat 1
$
vmstat 1
procs ---------memory---------- ---swap-- -----io---- -system-- ------cpu-----
r  b swpd   free   buff  cache   si   so    bi    bo   in   cs us sy id wa st
34  0    0 200889792  73708 591828    0    0     0     5    6   10 96  1  3  0  0
32  0    0 200889920  73708 591860    0    0     0   592 13284 4282 98  1  1  0  0
32  0    0 200890112  73708 591860    0    0     0     0 9501 2154 99  1  0  0  0
32  0    0 200889568  73712 591856    0    0     0    48 11900 2459 99  0  0  0  0
32  0    0 200890208  73712 591860    0    0     0     0 15898 4840 98  1  1  0  0
^C
Short for virtual memory stat, vmstat(8) is a commonly available tool (first created for BSD decades ago). It prints a summary of key server statistics on each line.
vmstat was run with an argument of 1, to print one second summaries. The first line of output (in this version of vmstat) has some columns that show the average since boot, instead of the previous second. For now, skip the first line, unless you want to learn and remember which column is which.
Columns to check:
r
: Number of processes running on CPU and waiting for a turn. This provides a better signal than load averages for determining CPU saturation, as it does not include I/O. To interpret: an “r” value greater than t
44722951.article_summary:
本文介绍了在Linux服务器上进行性能分析时，如何利用前60秒快速获取系统资源使用情况。通过运行十个标准Linux命令，可以初步了解系统性能问题。这些命令包括：

1. **uptime**：查看系统负载，了解CPU和I/O需求。
2. **dmesg | tail**：查看最近的系统消息，寻找错误。
3. **vmstat 1**：监控CPU、内存、I/O等资源的使用和饱和度。
4. **mpstat -P ALL 1**：查看每个CPU的使用情况。
5. **pidstat 1**：查看各个进程的资源使用情况。
6. **iostat -xz 1**：分析设备I/O性能。
7. **free -m**：查看内存使用情况。
8. **sar -n DEV 1**：监控网络接口。
9. **sar -n TCP,ETCP 1**：分析TCP和网络性能。
10. **top**：动态查看系统整体资源使用情况。

这些命令帮助快速识别系统资源（CPU、内存、磁盘等）的利用率、饱和度和错误，从而定位性能瓶颈。在Netflix的EC2 Linux环境中，这些工具对分析和解决问题至关重要。

data.title: The Hamming Question
data.author: eamag
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了“哈姆问题”（Hamming Question），即为什么人们不把精力投入到最重要的问题上。作者Raemon指出，对于有效利他主义（EA）群体来说，“重要”意味着对世界有实际影响，而学术界则通常以被认可的学术价值来定义“重要”。Vanessa Kosoy认为，随着某个问题投入的资源增多，其边际回报会减少，因此将精力转向被忽视的问题可能更有用。ChristianKl引用库恩的理论，指出追求实际应用的学科与追求学术认可的学科在进展上的差异。Raemon还担心一些AI安全研究人员可能会为了迎合外界期望而假装自己的工作与安全相关，从而造成一种虚假的安全感。总体而言，文章探讨了选择研究课题时的动机和实际影响之间的矛盾。

By the way, I never understood why it's supposed to be such a "trick" question. "Why aren't you working on them?" the obvious answer is, diminishing returns. If a lot of people (or a lot of "total IQ") already goes into problem X, then adding more to problem X might be less useful than adding more to problem Y, which is less important but also more neglected.
In the context of our community, people might interpret it as something like "why aren't more people working on mitigating X-risk instead of studying academic questions with no known applications", which
is
a good question, but it's not the same. The key here is the meaning of "important". For most academics, "important" means "acknowledged as important in the academia", or at best "intrinsically interesting". On the other hand, for EA-minded people "important" means "has actual positive influence on the world". This difference in the meaning of "important" seems much more important than blaming people for not choosing the
most
important question on a scale they already accept.

In medicine I think it's great for EA reasons when researchers do basic work that moves our understanding of the human body forward even when that doesn't have direct applications.

For one thing, this observation is strongly confounded by other characteristics that are different between those fields. For another, yes, I know that often something that was studied just for the love of knowledge has tremendous applications later. And yet, I feel that, if your goal is improving the world then there is room for more analysis than, "does it seem interesting to study that". Also what I consider "practical" is not necessarily what is normally viewed as "practical". For example I consider it "practical" to research a question because it may have some profound consequences many decades down the line, even if that's only backed by broad considerations rather than some concrete application.

Relatedly, rereading
this post
was what prompted me to write this stub post:
I'm fairly concerned with the practice of telling people who "really care about AI safety" to go into AI capabilities research, unless they are very junior researchers who are using general AI research as a place to improve their skills until they're able to contribute to AI safety later. (See
Leveraging Academia
).
The reason is not a fear that they will contribute to AI capabilities advancement in some manner that will be marginally detrimental to the future. It's also not a fear that they'll fail to change the company's culture in the ways they'd hope, and end up feeling discouraged. What I'm afraid of is that
they'll feel pressure to start pretending to themselves, or to others, that their work is "relevant to safety"
. Then what we end up with are companies and departments filled with people who are "concerned about safety", creating a false sense of security that something relevant is being done, when all we have are a bunch of simmering concerns and concomitant rationalizations.
This fear of mine requires some context from my background as a researcher. I see this problem with environmentalists who "really care about climate change", who tell themselves they're "working on it" by studying the roots of a fairly arbitrary species of tree in a fairly arbitrary ecosystem that won't generalize to anything likely to help with climate change.

data.title: The Convenience Trap: Why Seamless Banking Access Can Turn 2FA into 1FA
data.author: ocrb
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了多因素认证（MFA）在数字安全中的重要性及其面临的挑战。MFA依赖于用户提供两种或以上不同类型的证据来验证身份，通常包括：你知道的东西（密码）、你拥有的东西（设备）、以及你自身的东西（生物特征）。然而，现代追求“无缝用户体验”导致了许多MFA方法实际上将多种验证因素集中在一台设备（通常是智能手机）上，削弱了MFA的安全性。

文章分析了几种常见认证方法及其优缺点：
1. **手机银行应用与生物识别**：方便但非真正的双因素认证，若手机密码泄露，设备被盗后风险极高。
2. **基于SMS的令牌**：非常不安全，易受SIM卡交换等攻击，且通知镜像功能可能进一步破坏其安全性。
3. **无额外交互的认证应用**：易受设备被盗和恶意软件攻击。
4. **有额外交互的认证应用**：通过要求更多用户操作提升了安全性。

文章指出，过度追求便捷削弱了MFA应有的安全性，建议用户谨慎选择认证方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：双因素认证（2FA）及其在智能手机上的实现是否会退化为单因素认证（1FA），以及相关的安全性和便利性问题。

不同观点：
• [deredede] 认为文章描述的智能手机上的认证机制仍然是2FA，因为需要设备（你拥有的东西）和密码（你知道的东西）两个因素，而非单一的因素。
• [alistairSH] 指出在iPhone上，如果知道密码并添加新面孔到FaceID，所有使用FaceID的应用程序应强制重新认证，因此不同意文章中的观点。
• [jpc0] 强调即使密码被窥视并获取设备，这仍然是两个因素的失败，而不是退化为单一因素。类似于信用卡和PIN码的例子，两者都可以被攻击者获取，但这仍然是多因素认证。
• [AshamedCaptain] 提到在Android设备上，即使知道PIN并添加新指纹，所有应用程序会拒绝指纹认证，并需要手动重新注册，这使得1FA和2FA的结论有所不同。
• [pxeger1] 认为无论是使用生物识别（你是什么）和设备，还是设备和密码，都仍然是两个因素，攻击者需要更多的条件才能成功。
• [nerdjon] 质疑使用生物识别的情况下，PIN码被窥视是否真的会导致安全问题，因为生物识别本身已经减少了输入PIN的频率。同时提到软件基于的passkey也存在同样的问题。
• [frollogaston] 提出质疑，物理窃取Yubikey和窃取手机加密码没有本质区别，物理设备也可以被盗。
• [politelemon] 认为绑定到设备上的passkey不如绑定到物理安全密钥安全，批评将便利性置于安全性之上的做法。
• [dguest] 提到一些服务通过一次性密码实现2FA，但这种方法可以通过脚本自动化，从而降低安全性。
• [rkrisztian] 认为生物识别（如指纹、面部识别）本质上是不安全的，因为这些信息可以被轻易获取和复制，类似于用户名。
• [awhitby] 询问iOS中FaceID和密码认证是否可以被不同对待，并提到Apple的新功能"Stolen Device Protection"可以解决部分问题。
• [commandlinefan] 讽刺一些安全提示和用户界面设计不当，可能导致用户忽略真正的安全问题。
• [mindslight] 认为2FA在美国背景下是一个反功能，因为它增加了登录的复杂性，使得用户难以及时发现未经授权的交易。
• [OutOfHere] 认为passkey存在三个主要问题：不抗量子计算、供应商锁定、以及多账户支持问题。

补充讨论：

44724842.article_content:
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is the bedrock of modern digital security. Its principle is simple and powerful. As Wikipedia defines it, MFA is:
an electronic authentication method in which a user is granted access to a website or application only after successfully presenting two or more distinct types of evidence (or factors) to an authentication mechanism.
The key phrase here is
distinct types of evidence
. These factors are typically categorized as something you know (a password), something you have (a device), and something you are (a biometric). Any financial institution worth its salt implements MFA. Having opened many bank accounts in Switzerland, I’ve seen the full spectrum of authentication methods that are used here. They generally fall into one of these categories:
Mobile-only banking apps with phone biometrics
SMS-based tokens
Authenticator app without additional user interaction (simple push)
Authenticator app with additional user interaction (number matching, biometrics)
Separate hardware device or a physical code list
Passkeys
Unfortunately, the relentless drive for a “seamless user experience” has created a convenience trap. Many of these methods, while appearing distinct, collapse onto a single device: your smartphone. This consolidation fundamentally undermines the security promise of MFA, often degrading true two-factor authentication (
2
FA) into a fragile single-factor authentication (
1
FA).
Let’s analyze these methods against realistic threats that the average user faces:
Password Theft:
An attacker obtains your login credentials, for instance because a site is breached.
Phishing:
An attacker tricks you into authenticating on a malicious site.
Device Theft:
An attacker physically steals your smartphone.
Malware:
Your primary computer is compromised.
1. Mobile-only Banking Apps with Phone Biometrics
⌗
This is an increasingly popular model. You have a banking app on your phone, and you unlock it with the same biometrics (Face ID, fingerprint) you use to unlock the device itself.
While convenient, this is not true
2
FA. The “something you have” (the phone) and the “something you are” (your face/fingerprint) are often both gated by a single, weaker factor: the “something you know” (your device passcode). For instance on an iPhone, you can register a new face for FaceID if you know the passcode.
Thieves actively exploit this by “shoulder surfing” a victim’s iPhone passcode before stealing the device. As
reported by the Wall Street Journal
, once a thief has your passcode, they can easily enroll their own face in Face ID and gain full access to your digital life, including your banking apps. Apple’s “Stolen Device Protection” is a step in the right direction, but it’s a mitigating control that isn’t enabled by default for all users.
Protection against Device Theft:
Very poor if the passcode is also compromised.
Protection against Malware:
The security sandboxes of modern mobile operating systems are strong. However, new convenience features create new attack vectors. With macOS and iPhone Mirroring, malware on a compromised Mac could potentially view and interact with your banking app on the mirrored phone screen. If your banking PIN is also stored in a password manager accessible on that Mac, the entire security model crumbles.
2. SMS-based Tokens
⌗
SMS as a second factor is notoriously insecure and should have been deprecated years ago. It’s vulnerable to well-known attacks like SIM swapping, IMSI catchers, and flaws in the global SS7 telephony network. Despite this, there are unfortunately major financial institutions (e.g., Saxo Bank with $133B client assets) that still enable it by default.
Convenience features pour gasoline on this fire. With notification mirroring (a standard feature in Apple’s ecosystem), an SMS 2FA code sent to your phone instantly appears on your paired—and potentially compromised—laptop or tablet. This completely shatters the illusion that SMS is an “out-of-band” factor.
Protection against Device Theft:
Poor. A thief may be able to access the code without even unlocking the phone (depending on the notification settings). At least they still need the password for the bank account, but this may be available with the passcode (e.g. when it is stored in a password manager), resulting in the same threat as mobile-only banking apps.
Protection against Malware:
Can be flawed due to notification mirroring / similar features.
3. Authenticator App Without Additional User Interaction
⌗
This method sends a simple “Approve” or “Deny” prompt to your phone without requiring any other interaction from the user. Only a few banks in Switzerland use this method.
Like 1 and 2, this can be susceptible to device theft and malware depending on the configuration.
4. Authenticator App With Additional User Interaction
⌗
This is an improvement over 3 and used by most banks. Instead of a simple “Approve” button, the app requires a specific action on the phone that can’t be easily automa
44724842.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了多因素认证（MFA）在数字安全中的重要性及其面临的挑战。MFA依赖于用户提供两种或以上不同类型的证据来验证身份，通常包括：你知道的东西（密码）、你拥有的东西（设备）、以及你自身的东西（生物特征）。然而，现代追求“无缝用户体验”导致了许多MFA方法实际上将多种验证因素集中在一台设备（通常是智能手机）上，削弱了MFA的安全性。

文章分析了几种常见认证方法及其优缺点：
1. **手机银行应用与生物识别**：方便但非真正的双因素认证，若手机密码泄露，设备被盗后风险极高。
2. **基于SMS的令牌**：非常不安全，易受SIM卡交换等攻击，且通知镜像功能可能进一步破坏其安全性。
3. **无额外交互的认证应用**：易受设备被盗和恶意软件攻击。
4. **有额外交互的认证应用**：通过要求更多用户操作提升了安全性。

文章指出，过度追求便捷削弱了MFA应有的安全性，建议用户谨慎选择认证方法。
44724842.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：双因素认证（2FA）及其在智能手机上的实现是否会退化为单因素认证（1FA），以及相关的安全性和便利性问题。

不同观点：
• [deredede] 认为文章描述的智能手机上的认证机制仍然是2FA，因为需要设备（你拥有的东西）和密码（你知道的东西）两个因素，而非单一的因素。
• [alistairSH] 指出在iPhone上，如果知道密码并添加新面孔到FaceID，所有使用FaceID的应用程序应强制重新认证，因此不同意文章中的观点。
• [jpc0] 强调即使密码被窥视并获取设备，这仍然是两个因素的失败，而不是退化为单一因素。类似于信用卡和PIN码的例子，两者都可以被攻击者获取，但这仍然是多因素认证。
• [AshamedCaptain] 提到在Android设备上，即使知道PIN并添加新指纹，所有应用程序会拒绝指纹认证，并需要手动重新注册，这使得1FA和2FA的结论有所不同。
• [pxeger1] 认为无论是使用生物识别（你是什么）和设备，还是设备和密码，都仍然是两个因素，攻击者需要更多的条件才能成功。
• [nerdjon] 质疑使用生物识别的情况下，PIN码被窥视是否真的会导致安全问题，因为生物识别本身已经减少了输入PIN的频率。同时提到软件基于的passkey也存在同样的问题。
• [frollogaston] 提出质疑，物理窃取Yubikey和窃取手机加密码没有本质区别，物理设备也可以被盗。
• [politelemon] 认为绑定到设备上的passkey不如绑定到物理安全密钥安全，批评将便利性置于安全性之上的做法。
• [dguest] 提到一些服务通过一次性密码实现2FA，但这种方法可以通过脚本自动化，从而降低安全性。
• [rkrisztian] 认为生物识别（如指纹、面部识别）本质上是不安全的，因为这些信息可以被轻易获取和复制，类似于用户名。
• [awhitby] 询问iOS中FaceID和密码认证是否可以被不同对待，并提到Apple的新功能"Stolen Device Protection"可以解决部分问题。
• [commandlinefan] 讽刺一些安全提示和用户界面设计不当，可能导致用户忽略真正的安全问题。
• [mindslight] 认为2FA在美国背景下是一个反功能，因为它增加了登录的复杂性，使得用户难以及时发现未经授权的交易。
• [OutOfHere] 认为passkey存在三个主要问题：不抗量子计算、供应商锁定、以及多账户支持问题。

Founder
About the role
Who?
We are Sei, an AI-powered regulatory compliance platform. Since launching, a few months ago, we're live with large enterprises across the US, Europe, and APAC and growing at double digits per month.
We are backed by world-class investors including Y Combinator, Tribe Capital, PayPal, Picus Capital & Hashed. Pranay (CEO) and Ram (CTO) are the founders. We have combined experience of 20+ years of building fintech, and tech products for businesses & customers across the world at companies such as Deutsche Bank, Cloud Kitchens, PayPal, TransferWise, and Amazon, among others.
We are looking for a full-stack engineer who will help shape the tech, product, and culture of the company. We are currently working with a bunch of enterprise customers and banks and are experiencing rapid growth. We are looking to hire very senior engineers who can take our V1 into a more scaleable, robust platform as we prepare for more growth.
What to expect
The tech stack looks like the below (expect this to change as we scale):
Typescript for APIs
React with Next.js
Python scripts for AI/ML
AWS, GCP & Terraform
You can expect to do all of the following:
Build clean, concise APIs for customer integrations, along with the documentation
Setup, run, scale, and maintain infrastructure
Fool-proof security across the stack - encryption, hashing, privacy, VPC, etc.
Infrastructure as code - build terraform scripts and ensure easy replication of the infra across different regions
Manage production deployments, logging, and monitoring
Setup on-call processes
Mentor junior engineers
Our values
Continuous 360 feedback: Everyone is expected to share constructive critical feedback with everyone else, including the founders.
Product-minded: Everyone shares product ownership, so we expect everyone to do customer outreach, support, and talk to customers for feedback and new features.
Doers over talkers: We spend time figuring out the right direction to take and then execute very fast. No one is too “senior” to do a job - the CTO will code every day, the CEO will sell every day and everyone takes care of customer support on a schedule. We understand the difference between real work and pretense.
Humanity over everything else: We sell the product to businesses, but in reality, we sell it to real humans on the other side. Our end customers are consumers using the product through our UI or integrated with our APIs, so we are building the world’s most human-centric company (no pun intended). Kindness is expected and empathy is the core value we’re looking for.
About you
We expect you to have built things from 0 to 1 or 1 to 10. Experience with Typescript/NodeJS and React is mandatory.
We don’t read much into your CV, but rather see what you have done in your life so far (side projects, open-source contributions, blogs, etc.). We don’t care about degrees, the institutions you went to, or the companies you worked for before. We are open to talking as long as you have put in the reps, good judgment and clarity, align with our values, and have a strong track record of thoughtful work.
Understand the fundamentals of building and integrating APIs and secure systems. You can take ownership of the tech stack from infra to APIs and UIs and can optimize for both developer productivity and product performance.
We expect you to have worked with early-stage companies before (0 to 1 or 1 to 10), have an extremely strong bias for action, and have built and/or scaled systems from scratch.
We expect you to know about Generative AI and LLMs. An ideal candidate should have tinkered with different models and understand the different problems around hallucinations, token optimizations, etc.
Pay and benefits We offer a solid, competitive package (including early-stage equity). We give you the flexibility to choose the split between cash and equity.
Why you should not join
If you want to coast along and do the minimal possible work. The work hours will be intense - we believe in less micro-management and high accountability. It takes a lot of sweat to get a startup off the ground and you will let the team down if you don’t pull up the socks.
If you cannot do intense work every day (with exceptions of course). The above point talks about the sheer quantity of the work, but this one is more on the quality. We have intentionally kept meetings to a bare minimum, so people can get into their zones and be productive. But if this gets you distracted and you commit half-assed things, then we might not be the right fit for you.
If you have low ambition. We believe in hiring ambitious and hard-working folks who will never take

data.author: rbanffy

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JWST（詹姆斯·韦伯空间望远镜）的新发现及其对天文学理论的影响，以及相关的天文学概念和研究资金问题。

不同观点：
• jordanb认为JWST正在颠覆许多理论，带来了许多新发现，并对天文领域产生了巨大影响。他提到一个包含JWST十大发现的列表，但未包括"红点"（可能指某些特殊天文现象）。
• db48x和chasil提供了关于"黑洞星"（Black Hole Star）的资源，推荐了一个Kurzgesagt的视频，旨在帮助理解这一概念。
• BurningFrog和spacecadet偏离主题，提到Soundgarden乐队的一首歌名与科学概念巧合地相符，带有幽默和调侃的意味。
• jjbinx007提到"Blowtorch Theory"（喷灯理论），并询问这是否与讨论的主题相关，暗示可能存在理论上的联系。
• voxleone对引力红移和红颜色的关系提出质疑，认为尽管有其他解释（如AGN相关效应、多普勒展宽、红外尘埃再处理、宇宙学红移），但应考虑引力效应的贡献。
• ErigmolCt提出疑问，认为随着仪器进步，许多"已知"的天文学现象可能会被重新解释为完全不同的东西。
• vivzkestrel表达了对超光速旅行和空间压缩的愿望，认为即使实现瞬移，访问所有天体仍需无限时间，反映了对天文探索的渴望和现实限制的无奈。
• mosesbp批评当前政府对NSF和NASA的资助削减，认为这将限制天文学研究，特别是关于星系演化和黑洞增长的关键问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中包含了一些轻松的题外话，如对音乐和科学概念巧合的调侃。
• 引力红移和红颜色的关系是一个技术性较强的讨论点，voxleone对此提供了详细的背景。
• mosesbp提到了研究资金的政治背景，将讨论引向了科学研究资助问题。
• 不同评论者对新发现的影响、理论验证及技术可行性表达了各自看法，显示出对天文学进展的多角度关注。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议点在于天文学现象的解释和引力红移是否在某些发现中起作用。

data.author: BUFU
data.article_summary: Ollama推出了适用于macOS和Windows的新应用，用户可以更方便地下载和与模型聊天。该应用支持文件拖放功能，便于处理文本或PDF文件，并且可以通过调整设置增加上下文长度来处理大型文档（需更多内存）。此外，新应用还支持多模态功能，可向兼容模型发送图片，如Gemma 3模型。同时，模型也可以处理代码文件用于文档编写。用户可在Ollama官网或GitHub发布页面下载该应用或命令行版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ollama产品及其目标用户、功能、跨平台支持以及与其他LLM应用的比较

不同观点：
• [第一种观点] pentagrama认为Ollama的目标用户从开发者转向了普通用户，因为其官网和产品主页不再强调CLI版本，而是专注于GUI版本。他还提到其他本地LLM应用如LM Studio和Msty，并指出ChatGPT桌面应用的快捷键功能（Alt + Space）是一个值得借鉴的好功能。
